# Recipes

A recipe is a verified [`http`](plan-format.md#the-generic-http-adapter) spec for one operation of one provider,
shipped with Sponson: the line names it and fills in its params, and the requests, envelopes, ids and drift rules
come from the recipe. Everything the generic adapter guarantees holds unchanged (intents before creates, idempotent
apply, drift by hash, destroy only what Sponson created). Why and how: [ADR 0020](adr/0020-recipes.md).

```yaml
providers:
  http:
    cloudflare: { recipe: cloudflare }   # optional: the recipe's API defaults; override base_url, auth, headers here
changes:
  - id: preview_dns
    adapter: http
    op: resource                         # the recipe's kind: resource or list_item
    recipe: cloudflare.dns_cname
    zone_id: 023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353
    name: "${ctx.scope}.preview.example.com"
    target: preview-host.example.net
```

- `recipe: <provider>.<op>` picks the operation; `api` defaults to `<provider>`, and so does its block under
  `providers.http`: write the block only to override `base_url`, `base_url_env`, `auth`, `headers` or `encoding`.
- Every other key of the line is one of the recipe's params. Values are literals, `${ctx.*}`, `{ from }`,
  `{ secret }` or `{ keep: true }`, as anywhere in a plan. An unknown param, a missing required one or a value of
  the wrong type is `PARAM_INVALID` naming it, before any request; an unknown recipe or op lists the known ones.
- `destroy: keep` leaves what the line made in place when the scope is destroyed.
- Identity: the ledger records the API block as resolved (base URL, credential variable, headers, encoding) and the
  keys and record ids of the expanded requests, never the recipe's text. A line written by hand with the same
  values is the same resource, and a new Sponson version whose recipe changes only its docs, params or assumptions
  re-identifies nothing.

Every op below is tested by `scenarios/recipes.test.ts` against the local fake cloud (create, idempotent re-apply,
drift, destroy), and live with `pnpm test:live` when its credential and the `SPONSON_LIVE_*` variables its recipe
names are set.

## AWS Amplify Hosting

Recipe file: [`packages/adapters/recipes/amplify.yaml`](../packages/adapters/recipes/amplify.yaml). Verified on 2026-10-11 against:

- [CreateBranch](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amplify/latest/APIReference/API_CreateBranch.html)
- [GetBranch](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amplify/latest/APIReference/API_GetBranch.html)
- [UpdateBranch](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amplify/latest/APIReference/API_UpdateBranch.html)
- [DeleteBranch](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amplify/latest/APIReference/API_DeleteBranch.html)
- [Amplify endpoints and quotas](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/general/latest/gr/amplify.html)
- [Create a signed AWS API request (SigV4)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/reference_sigv-create-signed-request.html)

| API default | Value |
|---|---|
| `base_url` | `https://amplify.us-east-1.amazonaws.com` |
| `base_url_env` | `AMPLIFY_API_URL` |
| Credential | `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` / `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` (AWS SigV4, `amplify` in `us-east-1`) |

Assumptions:

- **AM1** (verified, [source](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/general/latest/gr/amplify.html)): The Amplify API is regional (`https://amplify.<region>.amazonaws.com`) and signed with SigV4 for the service `amplify`. The recipe defaults to `us-east-1`; an app in another region sets `base_url` and `auth` (with its `region`) in the provider block, and temporary credentials (a CI role) add `session_token_env: AWS_SESSION_TOKEN` there.
- **AM2** (verified, [source](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amplify/latest/APIReference/API_CreateBranch.html)): `POST /apps/{appId}/branches` (CreateBranch) creates a branch from `branchName` (required) and optional `description`, `stage` (PRODUCTION, BETA, DEVELOPMENT, EXPERIMENTAL, PULL_REQUEST), `enableAutoBuild`, `environmentVariables`, …; it answers 200 with `{ branch }`.
- **AM3** (verified, [source](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amplify/latest/APIReference/API_GetBranch.html)): `GET /apps/{appId}/branches/{branchName}` (GetBranch) answers `{ branch }` with `branchName`, `stage`, `description`, `enableAutoBuild` and `environmentVariables` (a map of string to string).
- **AM4** (verified, [source](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amplify/latest/APIReference/API_UpdateBranch.html)): `POST /apps/{appId}/branches/{branchName}` (UpdateBranch) takes the same optional fields and answers `{ branch }`; `environmentVariables` is the branch's whole map of variables.
- **AM5** (verified, [source](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amplify/latest/APIReference/API_DeleteBranch.html)): `DELETE /apps/{appId}/branches/{branchName}` (DeleteBranch) deletes a branch; an unknown app or branch is 404 `NotFoundException`.
- **AM6** **(unverified)**: UpdateBranch leaves the fields it is not sent as they are (so the branch op's update does not reset the variables, and the variable op's write does not reset the branch's settings), while an `environmentVariables` it is sent replaces the whole map, as the sim models it (assumption A4 of packages/sim/src/routes/aws.ts).
- **AM7** **(unverified)**: A build that ran before a variable was written does not see it: Sponson does not start a new job (StartJob), so order the variable lines before the branch's first build (`enable_auto_build: false` and a CI-started job, or the branch line, then the variables, then the push). The branches Amplify's own pull request previews make are not modelled; this recipe manages a branch the plan names.

### `amplify.branch`

**Branch** (`http.resource`). An Amplify branch named by the plan (the git branch of the pull request, `${ctx.git.branch}`), created with CreateBranch and deleted on destroy. Its `stage`, `description` and auto-build setting are compared: a console edit is drift. Variables on it are `amplify.branch_variable` lines.

Covers: `amplify-branch` in [the coverage matrix](coverage.md#coverage-matrix). Outputs: `id`. On destroy: deleted (`destroy: keep` on the line leaves it).

| Param | Type | Required | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `app_id` | string | yes | — | The Amplify app's id. Matches `^d[a-z0-9]+$`. |
| `branch_name` | string | yes | — | The branch's name, as the repository names it. |
| `stage` | string | no | — | The branch's stage. One of `PRODUCTION`, `BETA`, `DEVELOPMENT`, `EXPERIMENTAL`, `PULL_REQUEST`. |
| `description` | string | no | — | The branch's description. |
| `enable_auto_build` | boolean | no | — | Build automatically on every push (false lets CI start the build after the variables are written; AM7). |

```yaml
# under changes: (no provider block needed)
- id: branch
  adapter: http
  op: resource
  recipe: amplify.branch
  app_id: d1demo
  branch_name: ${ctx.scope}
  stage: PULL_REQUEST
  description: Preview of ${ctx.scope}
```

What the line expands into: the [`http.resource`](plan-format.md#httpresource) params, `{ param: <name> }` standing for a param's value and `{<name>}` in a path for its URI-encoded value.

```yaml
read:
  path: /apps/{app_id}/branches/{branch_name}
create:
  path: /apps/{app_id}/branches
  body:
    branchName: { param: branch_name }
update:
  method: POST
item_path: /branch
id_path: /branchName
fields:
  stage: { param: stage }
  description: { param: description }
  enableAutoBuild: { param: enable_auto_build }
```

### `amplify.branch_variable`

**Branch environment variable** (`http.list_item`). One entry of a branch's `environmentVariables`, by read-modify-write of the whole map (UpdateBranch replaces the map it is sent); other variables are left alone, and the branch is locked while Sponson writes it. A branch that is not there yet reads as having no variables, so a plan that also creates the branch shows a create. Builds started before the write do not see it (AM7).

Covers: `amplify-branch` in [the coverage matrix](coverage.md#coverage-matrix). Outputs: none. On destroy: deleted (`destroy: keep` on the line leaves it).

| Param | Type | Required | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `app_id` | string | yes | — | The Amplify app's id. Matches `^d[a-z0-9]+$`. |
| `branch_name` | string | yes | — | The branch's name (a `{ from }` of the `amplify.branch` line orders the two). |
| `name` | string | yes | — | The variable's name. |
| `value` | string | yes | — | The variable's value. |

```yaml
# under changes: (no provider block needed)
- id: branch_variable
  adapter: http
  op: list_item
  recipe: amplify.branch_variable
  app_id: d1demo
  branch_name: ${ctx.scope}
  name: API_URL
  value: https://api-${ctx.scope}.example.app
```

What the line expands into: the [`http.list_item`](plan-format.md#httplist_item) params, `{ param: <name> }` standing for a param's value and `{<name>}` in a path for its URI-encoded value.

```yaml
parent:
  path: /apps/{app_id}/branches/{branch_name}
  method: POST
  send: collection
  item_path: /branch
  if_missing: empty
list_path: /environmentVariables
shape: map
item: { param: name }
value: { param: value }
```

## Auth0

Recipe file: [`packages/adapters/recipes/auth0.yaml`](../packages/adapters/recipes/auth0.yaml). Verified on 2026-10-11 against:

- [Get Management API access tokens for production](https://auth0.com/docs/secure/tokens/access-tokens/management-api-access-tokens/get-management-api-access-tokens-for-production)
- [Management API v2, get a client](https://auth0.com/docs/api/management/v2/clients/get-clients-by-id)
- [Management API v2, update a client](https://auth0.com/docs/api/management/v2/clients/patch-clients-by-id)
- [Auth0 Terraform provider, configuration (conventional variable names)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/auth0/terraform-provider-auth0/main/docs/index.md)

| API default | Value |
|---|---|
| `base_url` | none: set it in the provider block |
| `base_url_env` | `AUTH0_API_URL` |
| Credential | `AUTH0_CLIENT_ID` / `AUTH0_CLIENT_SECRET` (OAuth2 client credentials) |
| Token endpoint | `/oauth/token` on the origin of `base_url`; override: `AUTH0_TOKEN_URL` |
| Audience | `/api/v2/` on the origin of `base_url` |

Assumptions:

- **AU1** (verified, [source](https://auth0.com/docs/secure/tokens/access-tokens/management-api-access-tokens/get-management-api-access-tokens-for-production)): A machine-to-machine application gets a Management API token from `POST https://<tenant>/oauth/token` (form-encoded `grant_type=client_credentials`, `client_id`, `client_secret`, `audience`); the audience is the Management API's identifier `https://<tenant>/api/v2/`. The answer has `access_token`, `expires_in` (86400 in the example) and `token_type: Bearer`. The recipe writes both as paths, so a plan's `base_url: https://<tenant>/api/v2` names the tenant once.
- **AU2** (verified, [source](https://auth0.com/docs/api/management/v2/clients/get-clients-by-id)): `GET /api/v2/clients/{id}` answers the application with its `callbacks`, `allowed_logout_urls`, `web_origins` and `allowed_origins` arrays, which only a token with `read:clients` (or `read:client_keys`) receives. `fields` with `include_fields=true` limits the answer to the listed fields, so the recipe never reads the client secret.
- **AU3** (verified, [source](https://auth0.com/docs/api/management/v2/clients/patch-clients-by-id)): `PATCH /api/v2/clients/{id}` (scope `update:clients`) updates an application; `callbacks`, `allowed_logout_urls`, `web_origins` and `allowed_origins` are arrays of strings, and the body needs at least one property, so a write sends the one array alone.
- **AU4** **(unverified)**: An array sent in a PATCH replaces the stored array whole (it is not merged), so the recipe sends the full list read just before with one URL added or removed. The reference does not say so for these fields.
- **AU5** **(unverified)**: Updates have no precondition (no ETag or version): the line locks the application (`lockOn`, one lock per tenant and client id, shared by the four ops) against other Sponson runs, and a console edit made between the read and the write can still be lost (the next apply then reports it as drift).
- **AU6** **(unverified)**: URLs are stored and read back exactly as written (no trailing slash added or case changed), so a URL identifies its entry.
- **AU7** (verified, [source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/auth0/terraform-provider-auth0/main/docs/index.md)): `AUTH0_CLIENT_ID` and `AUTH0_CLIENT_SECRET` are the variables the Auth0 Terraform provider reads for a machine-to-machine client.
- **AU8** **(unverified)**: The audience stays the tenant's canonical domain when the tenant has a custom domain, so `base_url` names the canonical domain (`<tenant>.<region>.auth0.com`), not the custom one.

### `auth0.callback_url`

**Application callback URL** (`http.list_item`). One URL in an Auth0 application's Allowed Callback URLs (`callbacks`), such as the preview's `/callback`; usually `{ from: <deploy line>.preview_url }` joined with the path in the app. Added by read-modify-write of the list under a lock on the application, removed on destroy; every other URL is left as it is. A URL removed in the Dashboard is drift (`missing`) that the next apply puts back.

Covers: `auth0-callbacks` in [the coverage matrix](coverage.md#coverage-matrix). Outputs: none. On destroy: deleted (`destroy: keep` on the line leaves it).

| Param | Type | Required | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `client_id` | string | yes | — | The application's Client ID. |
| `url` | string | yes | — | The callback URL, exactly as the application sends it as `redirect_uri`. Matches `^https?://\\S+$`. |

```yaml
providers:
  http:
    auth0:
      recipe: auth0
      base_url: https://acme.eu.auth0.com/api/v2
changes:
  - id: callback_url
    adapter: http
    op: list_item
    recipe: auth0.callback_url
    client_id: AbC123dEf456GhI789jKl012MnO345pQ
    url: https://${ctx.scope}.preview.example.app/callback
```

What the line expands into: the [`http.list_item`](plan-format.md#httplist_item) params, `{ param: <name> }` standing for a param's value and `{<name>}` in a path for its URI-encoded value.

```yaml
parent:
  path: /clients/{client_id}
  read_path: /clients/{client_id}?fields=callbacks,allowed_logout_urls,web_origins,allowed_origins&include_fields=true
list_path: /callbacks
item: { param: url }
```

### `auth0.logout_url`

**Application allowed logout URL** (`http.list_item`). One URL in an Auth0 application's Allowed Logout URLs (`allowed_logout_urls`), where `/v2/logout` may return the user, such as the preview's home page. Read-modify-write of the list under the application's lock; removed on destroy; every other URL is left as it is.

Covers: `auth0-callbacks` in [the coverage matrix](coverage.md#coverage-matrix). Outputs: none. On destroy: deleted (`destroy: keep` on the line leaves it).

| Param | Type | Required | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `client_id` | string | yes | — | The application's Client ID. |
| `url` | string | yes | — | The URL the application passes as `returnTo` on logout. Matches `^https?://\\S+$`. |

```yaml
providers:
  http:
    auth0:
      recipe: auth0
      base_url: https://acme.eu.auth0.com/api/v2
changes:
  - id: logout_url
    adapter: http
    op: list_item
    recipe: auth0.logout_url
    client_id: AbC123dEf456GhI789jKl012MnO345pQ
    url: https://${ctx.scope}.preview.example.app
```

What the line expands into: the [`http.list_item`](plan-format.md#httplist_item) params, `{ param: <name> }` standing for a param's value and `{<name>}` in a path for its URI-encoded value.

```yaml
parent:
  path: /clients/{client_id}
  read_path: /clients/{client_id}?fields=callbacks,allowed_logout_urls,web_origins,allowed_origins&include_fields=true
list_path: /allowed_logout_urls
item: { param: url }
```

### `auth0.web_origin`

**Application allowed web origin** (`http.list_item`). One origin in an Auth0 application's Allowed Web Origins (`web_origins`), which silent authentication and the SPA SDKs' token refresh need for the preview's origin. Read-modify-write of the list under the application's lock; removed on destroy; every other origin is left as it is.

Covers: `auth0-callbacks` in [the coverage matrix](coverage.md#coverage-matrix). Outputs: none. On destroy: deleted (`destroy: keep` on the line leaves it).

## Azure Static Web Apps

Recipe file: [`packages/adapters/recipes/azure_swa.yaml`](../packages/adapters/recipes/azure_swa.yaml). Verified on 2026-10-11 against:

- [Static Sites - Create Or Update Static Site Build App Settings](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/rest/api/appservice/static-sites/create-or-update-static-site-build-app-settings?view=rest-appservice-2024-04-01)
- [Static Sites - List Static Site Build App Settings](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/rest/api/appservice/static-sites/list-static-site-build-app-settings?view=rest-appservice-2024-04-01)
- [Static Sites - Get Static Site Builds](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/rest/api/appservice/static-sites/get-static-site-builds?view=rest-appservice-2024-04-01)
- [Preview environments in Azure Static Web Apps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/static-web-apps/preview-environments)
- [Configure application settings for Azure Static Web Apps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/static-web-apps/application-settings)
- [az account get-access-token](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/cli/azure/account#az-account-get-access-token)

| API default | Value |
|---|---|
| `base_url` | `https://management.azure.com` |
| `base_url_env` | `AZURE_SWA_API_URL` |
| Credential | the token `az account get-access-token --query accessToken -o tsv` prints (bearer) |

Assumptions:

- **AZ1** (verified, [source](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/rest/api/appservice/static-sites/create-or-update-static-site-build-app-settings?view=rest-appservice-2024-04-01)): `PUT https://management.azure.com/subscriptions/{subscriptionId}/resourceGroups/{resourceGroupName}/providers/Microsoft.Web/staticSites/{name}/builds/{environmentName}/config/appsettings?api-version=2024-04-01` with `{ properties: { <name>: <value>, … } }` sets the app settings of one environment (build) and answers 200 with the same `properties`.
- **AZ2** (verified, [source](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/rest/api/appservice/static-sites/list-static-site-build-app-settings?view=rest-appservice-2024-04-01)): The settings are read with `POST …/builds/{environmentName}/listAppSettings?api-version=2024-04-01` (no body), which answers a StringDictionary `{ id, properties }`; there is no GET, so the recipe reads with `parent.read_method: POST`.
- **AZ3** (verified, [source](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/rest/api/appservice/static-sites/get-static-site-builds?view=rest-appservice-2024-04-01)): Each environment is a `builds/{environmentName}` resource: production is `default`, a pull request's preview environment is named by the pull request's number (`builds/12`).
- **AZ4** (verified, [source](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/static-web-apps/preview-environments)): A preview environment exists from the pull request's first deployment and is deleted, with its settings, when the pull request is closed; app settings reach the app's managed API (Functions), not the front-end build.
- **AZ5** (verified, [source](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/cli/azure/account#az-account-get-access-token)): `az account get-access-token --query accessToken -o tsv` prints an Azure Resource Manager access token for the signed-in account (the default resource is `https://management.azure.com/`), sent as a bearer token.
- **AZ6** **(unverified)**: The PUT replaces the whole settings map (a setting it is not sent is removed), so the recipe sends the map as read with the one entry changed (`send: collection`); there is no ETag on this resource, so only Sponson's own writers are serialised (the parent lock), and a setting added in the portal between the read and the write is lost.
- **AZ7** **(unverified)**: Listing the settings of an environment that does not exist (not deployed yet, or deleted with its pull request) answers 404, which the recipe reads as no settings (`if_missing: empty`): plan shows a create before the first deploy, and destroy after the pull request closed is a no-op. A write before the first deploy fails with that 404; order the line after the deploy.

### `azure_swa.build_app_setting`

**App setting of a preview environment** (`http.list_item`). One app setting of a Static Web App environment (a pull request's preview environment is named by its number), by read-modify-write of the environment's settings: read with `listAppSettings`, written whole with a PUT. Other settings are left alone and the environment is locked while Sponson writes it. Settings reach the app's managed API, not the front-end build (AZ4); the environment exists only after the PR's first deploy (AZ7).

Covers: `azure-swa-settings` in [the coverage matrix](coverage.md#coverage-matrix). Outputs: none. On destroy: deleted (`destroy: keep` on the line leaves it).

| Param | Type | Required | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `subscription_id` | string | yes | — | The Azure subscription id. |
| `resource_group` | string | yes | — | The resource group of the static web app. |
| `site` | string | yes | — | The static web app's name. |
| `environment` | string | yes | — | The environment's name (the pull request's number for its preview environment; `default` is production). Matches `^[a-zA-Z0-9]+$`. |
| `name` | string | yes | — | The setting's name. |
| `value` | string | yes | — | The setting's value. |

```yaml
# under changes: (no provider block needed)
- id: build_app_setting
  adapter: http
  op: list_item
  recipe: azure_swa.build_app_setting
  subscription_id: 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000
  resource_group: rg-web
  site: web
  environment: "42"
  name: API_URL
  value: https://api-${ctx.scope}.example.app
```

What the line expands into: the [`http.list_item`](plan-format.md#httplist_item) params, `{ param: <name> }` standing for a param's value and `{<name>}` in a path for its URI-encoded value.

```yaml
parent:
  path: /subscriptions/{subscription_id}/resourceGroups/{resource_group}/providers/Microsoft.Web/staticSites/{site}/builds/{environment}/config/appsettings?api-version=2024-04-01
  read_path: /subscriptions/{subscription_id}/resourceGroups/{resource_group}/providers/Microsoft.Web/staticSites/{site}/builds/{environment}/listAppSettings?api-version=2024-04-01
  read_method: POST
  method: PUT
  send: collection
  if_missing: empty
list_path: /properties
shape: map
item: { param: name }
value: { param: value }
```

## Google Cloud Run

Recipe file: [`packages/adapters/recipes/cloud_run.yaml`](../packages/adapters/recipes/cloud_run.yaml). Verified on 2026-10-11 against:

- [REST Resource: projects.locations.services (Service, TrafficTarget)](https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/reference/rest/v2/projects.locations.services)
- [Method: projects.locations.services.patch](https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/reference/rest/v2/projects.locations.services/patch)
- [Method: projects.locations.services.get](https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/reference/rest/v2/projects.locations.services/get)
- [Rollbacks, gradual rollouts, and traffic migration (tags)](https://cloud.google.com/run/docs/rollouts-rollbacks-traffic-migration)
- [gcloud auth print-access-token](https://cloud.google.com/sdk/gcloud/reference/auth/print-access-token)

| API default | Value |
|---|---|
| `base_url` | `https://run.googleapis.com/v2` |
| `base_url_env` | `CLOUD_RUN_API_URL` |
| Credential | the token `gcloud auth print-access-token` prints (bearer) |

Assumptions:

- **CR1** (verified, [source](https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/reference/rest/v2/projects.locations.services)): `GET https://run.googleapis.com/v2/projects/{project}/locations/{location}/services/{service}` answers the Service with its `traffic` list and an `etag`, 'a system-generated fingerprint for this version of the resource' that 'may be used to detect modification conflict during updates'.
- **CR2** (verified, [source](https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/reference/rest/v2/projects.locations.services/patch)): `PATCH https://run.googleapis.com/v2/{service.name}` takes a Service and an optional `updateMask` (fields to update), answers a long-running Operation, and needs the `cloud-platform` scope; the recipe sends `?updateMask=traffic` with `{ traffic, etag }` only, so the revision template is never written.
- **CR3** (verified, [source](https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/reference/rest/v2/projects.locations.services)): A TrafficTarget is `{ type, revision, percent, tag }`; `type: TRAFFIC_TARGET_ALLOCATION_TYPE_REVISION` sends traffic to the named `revision`, `percent` defaults to zero, and `tag` is 'a string to be part of the URI to exclusively reference this target', which is the per-PR URL.
- **CR4** (verified, [source](https://cloud.google.com/sdk/gcloud/reference/auth/print-access-token)): `gcloud auth print-access-token` prints an OAuth access token for the active account, sent as a bearer token.
- **CR5** **(unverified)**: A patch whose `etag` no longer matches (a deploy changed the service after the read) is refused (409 ABORTED or 412) rather than applied: the line fails and the next apply reads again, so a concurrent `gcloud run deploy` is never overwritten. Sponson's own writers are serialised by the parent lock.
- **CR6** **(unverified)**: The Service answered right after the patch's Operation is accepted already shows the new `traffic` (the desired state), so the re-read that confirms the write sees the tag; `percent` 0 is left out of the answer and `type` and `revision` are answered as sent.
- **CR7** **(unverified)**: The revision a tag points to exists before the line applies: the PR's deploy creates it (`gcloud run deploy --no-traffic --revision-suffix <scope>` gives `<service>-<scope>`). Its environment variables are part of that revision, set by the deploy, not by this recipe; a deploy that tags (`--tag`) itself conflicts with this line's tag.

### `cloud_run.traffic_tag`

**Traffic tag of a revision** (`http.list_item`). A tag (`pr-42`) in a service's `traffic` list pointing at the PR's revision with no traffic share, which gives the revision its own URL (`https://pr-42---<service>-<hash>.a.run.app`). Read-modify-write of `traffic` only (`updateMask=traffic`), sent with the service's `etag` so a concurrent deploy makes the write fail instead of being overwritten (CR5); other tags and the traffic split are left alone, and destroy removes only this tag. The revision itself, and its environment variables, are the deploy's (CR7).

Covers: — in [the coverage matrix](coverage.md#coverage-matrix). Outputs: none. On destroy: deleted (`destroy: keep` on the line leaves it).

| Param | Type | Required | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `project` | string | yes | — | The Google Cloud project id. |
| `region` | string | yes | — | The service's region. |
| `service` | string | yes | — | The Cloud Run service's name. |
| `tag` | string | yes | — | The tag, the prefix of the revision's own URL. Matches `^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$`. |
| `revision` | string | yes | — | The revision the tag points to (made by the PR's deploy). |

```yaml
# under changes: (no provider block needed)
- id: traffic_tag
  adapter: http
  op: list_item
  recipe: cloud_run.traffic_tag
  project: demo-project
  region: us-central1
  service: web
  tag: ${ctx.scope}
  revision: web-${ctx.scope}
```

What the line expands into: the [`http.list_item`](plan-format.md#httplist_item) params, `{ param: <name> }` standing for a param's value and `{<name>}` in a path for its URI-encoded value.

```yaml
parent:
  path: /projects/{project}/locations/{region}/services/{service}?updateMask=traffic
  read_path: /projects/{project}/locations/{region}/services/{service}
  method: PATCH
  send:
    - etag
list_path: /traffic
key_field: tag
item:
  tag: { param: tag }
  revision: { param: revision }
  type: TRAFFIC_TARGET_ALLOCATION_TYPE_REVISION
```

## Cloudflare

Recipe file: [`packages/adapters/recipes/cloudflare.yaml`](../packages/adapters/recipes/cloudflare.yaml). Verified on 2026-10-11 against:

- [Create DNS record](https://developers.cloudflare.com/api/resources/dns/subresources/records/methods/create/)
- [List DNS records](https://developers.cloudflare.com/api/resources/dns/subresources/records/methods/list/)
- [DNS record details](https://developers.cloudflare.com/api/resources/dns/subresources/records/methods/get/)
- [Update DNS record (PATCH)](https://developers.cloudflare.com/api/resources/dns/subresources/records/methods/edit/)
- [Delete DNS record](https://developers.cloudflare.com/api/resources/dns/subresources/records/methods/delete/)

| API default | Value |
|---|---|
| `base_url` | `https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4` |
| `base_url_env` | `CLOUDFLARE_API_URL` |
| Credential | `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` (bearer) |

Assumptions:

- **CF1** (verified, [source](https://developers.cloudflare.com/api/resources/dns/subresources/records/methods/create/)): Records are created with `POST /zones/{zone_id}/dns_records` (`type`, `name`, `content`, `ttl`, `proxied`, `comment`), authenticated with an API token as `Authorization: Bearer` that has DNS Write on the zone.
- **CF2** (verified, [source](https://developers.cloudflare.com/api/resources/dns/subresources/records/methods/list/)): `GET /zones/{zone_id}/dns_records` answers `{ result: [...] }` and filters by `type` and `name.exact` (names compare case-insensitively).
- **CF3** (verified, [source](https://developers.cloudflare.com/api/resources/dns/subresources/records/methods/get/)): Single-record answers (create, details, update) carry the record under `result`, with its `id`.
- **CF4** (verified, [source](https://developers.cloudflare.com/api/resources/dns/subresources/records/methods/delete/)): `PATCH /zones/{zone_id}/dns_records/{id}` updates a record; `DELETE` on the same path removes it permanently.
- **CF5** **(unverified)**: A PATCH needs `name` and `type` alongside the changed fields (the edit schema does not mark them optional), so every update sends both.
- **CF6** **(unverified)**: The API returns `name` lower-cased as the full name and `content` as written, so `name` must be given lower-case and fully qualified, or every plan finds no record and tries to create one.
- **CF7** **(unverified)**: A proxied record reports `ttl: 1` (automatic) whatever was sent, so `ttl` other than 1 with `proxied: true` shows as drift on every plan.
- **CF8** (verified, [source](https://developers.cloudflare.com/api/resources/dns/subresources/records/methods/create/)): A CNAME cannot share its name with another record, so name and type identify it within the zone and a filtered list holds at most one, on its first page.

### `cloudflare.dns_cname`

**DNS CNAME record** (`http.resource`). A CNAME record in a zone, such as `pr-42.preview.example.com` pointing at the preview deployment's host. Located by name and type; a console edit of its target, proxying, TTL or comment is drift.

Covers: `cloudflare-dns` in [the coverage matrix](coverage.md#coverage-matrix). Outputs: `id`, `hostname`. On destroy: deleted (`destroy: keep` on the line leaves it).

| Param | Type | Required | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `zone_id` | string | yes | — | The zone's id (32 hex characters, on the zone's Overview page). Matches `^[0-9a-f]{32}$`. |
| `name` | string | yes | — | The record's full name, lower-case, zone included. Matches `^[a-z0-9*_.-]+$`. |
| `target` | string | yes | — | The host the name points at (the record's `content`). |
| `proxied` | boolean | no | `false` | Whether Cloudflare proxies the traffic. |
| `ttl` | integer | no | `1` | TTL in seconds (60–86400), or 1 for automatic. |
| `comment` | string | no | — | A note on the record; no effect on DNS. |

```yaml
# under changes: (no provider block needed)
- id: dns_cname
  adapter: http
  op: resource
  recipe: cloudflare.dns_cname
  zone_id: 023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353
  name: ${ctx.scope}.preview.example.com
  target: preview-host.example.net
  comment: Managed by Sponson
```

What the line expands into: the [`http.resource`](plan-format.md#httpresource) params, `{ param: <name> }` standing for a param's value and `{<name>}` in a path for its URI-encoded value.

```yaml
find:
  path: /zones/{zone_id}/dns_records?type=CNAME&name.exact={name}
  list_path: /result
  match:
    type: CNAME
    name: { param: name }
create:
  path: /zones/{zone_id}/dns_records
update:
  method: PATCH
  path: /zones/{zone_id}/dns_records/{id}
  body:
    type: CNAME
    name: { param: name }
delete:
  path: /zones/{zone_id}/dns_records/{id}
item_path: /result
fields:
  content: { param: target }
  proxied: { param: proxied }
  ttl: { param: ttl }
  comment: { param: comment }
outputs:
  hostname: /name
```

## CockroachDB Cloud

Recipe file: [`packages/adapters/recipes/cockroachdb.yaml`](../packages/adapters/recipes/cockroachdb.yaml). Verified on 2026-10-11 against:

- [Cloud API OpenAPI document (version 2026-09-15)](https://cockroachlabs.cloud/assets/docs/api/latest/openapi.json)
- [Use the CockroachDB Cloud API](https://docs.cockroachlabs.com/docs/cockroachcloud/cloud-api)

| API default | Value |
|---|---|
| `base_url` | `https://cockroachlabs.cloud/api/v1` |
| `base_url_env` | `COCKROACH_API_URL` |
| Credential | `COCKROACH_API_KEY` (bearer) |
| `headers` | {"Cc-Version":"2024-09-16"} |

Assumptions:

- **CR1** (verified, [source](https://docs.cockroachlabs.com/docs/cockroachcloud/cloud-api)): The Cloud API authenticates with a service account's secret key as `Authorization: Bearer`; the key has the service account's roles.
- **CR2** (verified, [source](https://docs.cockroachlabs.com/docs/cockroachcloud/cloud-api)): `Cc-Version` pins the API version (`YYYY-MM-DD`); without it the latest version answers, which may change under a client. The guide documents `2024-09-16`.
- **CR3** (verified, [source](https://cockroachlabs.cloud/assets/docs/api/latest/openapi.json)): `POST /clusters/{cluster_id}/databases` with `{ name }` creates a database and answers `{ name, table_count }`; `GET` on the same path lists `{ databases: [{ name, table_count }], pagination: { next_page } }`, paged with `pagination.page`; `DELETE /clusters/{cluster_id}/databases/{name}` deletes one. There is no GET of a single database.
- **CR4** (verified, [source](https://cockroachlabs.cloud/assets/docs/api/latest/openapi.json)): `POST /clusters/{cluster_id}/sql-users` with `{ name, password }` (both required) creates a SQL user; `GET` on the same path lists `{ users: [{ name }], pagination: { next_page } }`; `DELETE /clusters/{cluster_id}/sql-users/{name}` deletes one. The password cannot be read back; `PUT …/sql-users/{name}/password` changes it.
- **CR5** (verified, [source](https://docs.cockroachlabs.com/docs/cockroachcloud/cloud-api)): A SQL user created through the API gets the SQL `admin` role by default, which the guide advises against for anything but administration.
- **CR6** (verified, [source](https://cockroachlabs.cloud/assets/docs/api/latest/openapi.json)): Creating or deleting databases and SQL users needs a cluster-level role of the service account (Cluster Admin, Cluster Operator or Cluster Data Accessor for databases; Cluster Admin for SQL users).
- **CR7** **(unverified)**: `COCKROACH_API_KEY` is the variable the CockroachDB Terraform provider and `ccloud` read the key from.
- **CR8** **(unverified)**: A second create of an existing database or SQL user is refused with 409 (ALREADY_EXISTS), and deleting one that is gone answers 404.
- **CR9** **(unverified)**: Deleting a database drops it with its tables (CASCADE); the API offers no way to refuse when it holds data.
- **CR10** **(unverified)**: The API takes database and user names that need quoting in SQL (`app_pr-42`, from a scope with `-`) and quotes them itself.

### `cockroachdb.database`

**Database in a cluster** (`http.resource`). A database per scope in a shared CockroachDB Cloud cluster, such as `app_pr_42`, instead of a cluster per preview. Located by its name in the cluster's list; only its existence is compared (the API exposes nothing else to set); destroy drops it with its data (CR9).

Covers: `cockroachdb-database` in [the coverage matrix](coverage.md#coverage-matrix). Outputs: `id`. On destroy: deleted (`destroy: keep` on the line leaves it).

| Param | Type | Required | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `cluster_id` | string | yes | — | The cluster's id (a UUID, shown in the Cloud Console's URL). |
| `name` | string | yes | — | The database's name; its identity. A name with `-` (a scope such as `pr-42`) needs quoting in SQL (CR10). Matches `^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_.-]{0,62}$`. |

```yaml
# under changes: (no provider block needed)
- id: database
  adapter: http
  op: resource
  recipe: cockroachdb.database
  cluster_id: 9e3f1a52-63d1-4a4c-9b8f-2c8b7a0e5d11
  name: app_${ctx.scope}
```

What the line expands into: the [`http.resource`](plan-format.md#httpresource) params, `{ param: <name> }` standing for a param's value and `{<name>}` in a path for its URI-encoded value.

```yaml
find:
  path: /clusters/{cluster_id}/databases
  list_path: /databases
  match:
    name: { param: name }
  next: /pagination/next_page
  cursor_param: pagination.page
create:
  path: /clusters/{cluster_id}/databases
delete:
  path: /clusters/{cluster_id}/databases/{id}
id_path: /name
```

### `cockroachdb.sql_user`

**SQL user in a cluster** (`http.resource`). A SQL user per scope in a shared CockroachDB Cloud cluster, such as `app_pr_42`, with its password as an input (`{ secret: … }`, or a sensitive output of another line), sent on create only and never compared. It gets the SQL `admin` role (CR5): grant narrower privileges in SQL if previews must not administer the cluster. Located by its name; destroy deletes the user.

Covers: — in [the coverage matrix](coverage.md#coverage-matrix). Outputs: `id`. On destroy: deleted (`destroy: keep` on the line leaves it).

| Param | Type | Required | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `cluster_id` | string | yes | — | The cluster's id (a UUID, shown in the Cloud Console's URL). |
| `name` | string | yes | — | The user's name; its identity. Matches `^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_.-]{0,62}$`. |
| `password` | string | yes | — | The user's password, as a reference (`{ secret: env://… }`, or `{ from: <line>.<output> }` of a sensitive output); sent on create only (CR4). |

```yaml
# under changes: (no provider block needed)
- id: sql_user
  adapter: http
  op: resource
  recipe: cockroachdb.sql_user
```

## ConfigCat

Recipe file: [`packages/adapters/recipes/configcat.yaml`](../packages/adapters/recipes/configcat.yaml). Verified on 2026-10-11 against:

- [Public Management API](https://api.configcat.com/docs/)
- [OpenAPI spec (get value v2, replace value v2, targeting rule models)](https://api.configcat.com/docs/v1/swagger.json)
- [Terraform provider (credential variable names)](https://github.com/configcat/terraform-provider-configcat/blob/main/docs/index.md)

| API default | Value |
|---|---|
| `base_url` | `https://api.configcat.com` |
| `base_url_env` | `CONFIGCAT_API_URL` |
| Credential | `CONFIGCAT_BASIC_AUTH_USERNAME` / `CONFIGCAT_BASIC_AUTH_PASSWORD` (basic) |

Assumptions:

- **CC1** (verified, [source](https://api.configcat.com/docs/v1/swagger.json)): The API is at `https://api.configcat.com`, authenticated with Basic auth from Public API credentials (the Terraform provider's `CONFIGCAT_BASIC_AUTH_USERNAME` / `CONFIGCAT_BASIC_AUTH_PASSWORD`).
- **CC2** (verified, [source](https://api.configcat.com/docs/v1/swagger.json)): `GET /v2/environments/{environmentId}/settings/{settingId}/value` answers the setting's value in the environment bare: `defaultValue`, `targetingRules`, `percentageEvaluationAttribute` and read-only fields.
- **CC3** (verified, [source](https://api.configcat.com/docs/v1/swagger.json)): `PUT` on the same path replaces the value: only `defaultValue`, `targetingRules` and `percentageEvaluationAttribute` can be set, and one not sent is reset. So those three are sent, as read, with the rule list changed (`parent.send`).
- **CC4** (verified, [source](https://api.configcat.com/docs/v1/swagger.json)): A targeting rule is `{ conditions: [{ userCondition: { comparisonAttribute, comparator, comparisonValue: { stringValue, doubleValue, listValue: [{ value, hint }] } } }], value | percentageOptions }`; rules have no id and are evaluated in order. `isOneOf` and `sensitiveIsOneOf` compare a user attribute with a list.
- **CC5** (verified, [source](https://api.configcat.com/docs/v1/swagger.json)): Answers carry every member of a value (`boolValue`, `stringValue`, `intValue`, `doubleValue`, `predefinedVariationId`) and of a comparison value, the unused ones null; the rule is written with the same nulls so that it reads back equal.
- **CC6** **(unverified)**: A condition is read back with `segmentCondition` and `prerequisiteFlagCondition` null and each list value's `hint` null, exactly as written; otherwise every plan shows the rule as changed.
- **CC7** **(unverified)**: In a product with "Config changes require a reason" or approvals turned on, the PUT without `reason` / `bypassApproval` is refused (the query parameters are not sent); the apply then fails.

### `configcat.targeting_rule`

**Feature flag targeting rule** (`http.list_item`). A targeting rule on a boolean feature flag in one environment that serves a value to the preview, such as `IF Preview IS ONE OF [pr-42] THEN true`. Added after the flag's other rules (evaluated in order: an earlier matching rule wins); the default value and the other rules are written back as read. Identified by the matched value; a console edit of its condition or served value is drift. Destroy removes the rule.

Covers: `configcat-rule` in [the coverage matrix](coverage.md#coverage-matrix). Outputs: none. On destroy: deleted (`destroy: keep` on the line leaves it).

| Param | Type | Required | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `environment_id` | string | yes | — | The environment's id (a UUID). |
| `setting_id` | string | yes | — | The feature flag's numeric setting id. Matches `^[0-9]+$`. |
| `attribute` | string | yes | — | The user attribute the rule compares (a custom attribute such as `Preview`, or `Identifier`, `Email`). |
| `comparator` | string | no | `isOneOf` | `isOneOf`, or `sensitiveIsOneOf` (hashed in the config JSON). One of `isOneOf`, `sensitiveIsOneOf`. |
| `match` | string | yes | — | The attribute value that is the preview; it identifies the rule. |
| `serve` | boolean | no | `true` | The value the flag serves to the preview. |

```yaml
# under changes: (no provider block needed)
- id: targeting_rule
  adapter: http
  op: list_item
  recipe: configcat.targeting_rule
  environment_id: 08d8becf-d4d9-4c66-8b48-6ac74cd95fba
  setting_id: "12345"
  attribute: Preview
  match: ${ctx.scope}
```

What the line expands into: the [`http.list_item`](plan-format.md#httplist_item) params, `{ param: <name> }` standing for a param's value and `{<name>}` in a path for its URI-encoded value.

```yaml
parent:
  path: /v2/environments/{environment_id}/settings/{setting_id}/value
  method: PUT
  send:
    - defaultValue
    - percentageEvaluationAttribute
list_path: /targetingRules
key_field: /conditions/0/userCondition/comparisonValue/listValue/0/value
item:
  conditions:
    - userCondition:
        comparisonAttribute: { param: attribute }
        comparator: { param: comparator }
        comparisonValue:
          stringValue: null
          doubleValue: null
          listValue:
            - value: { param: match }
              hint: null
      segmentCondition: null
      prerequisiteFlagCondition: null
  value:
    boolValue: { param: serve }
    stringValue: null
    intValue: null
    doubleValue: null
    predefinedVariationId: null
```

## Datadog

Recipe file: [`packages/adapters/recipes/datadog.yaml`](../packages/adapters/recipes/datadog.yaml). Verified on 2026-10-11 against:

- [Synthetics API reference](https://docs.datadoghq.com/api/latest/synthetics/)
- [API authentication (keys, sites)](https://docs.datadoghq.com/api/latest/authentication/)
- [Datadog API v1 OpenAPI document (datadog-api-client)](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-api-client-typescript/blob/master/.generator/schemas/v1/openapi.yaml)

| API default | Value |
|---|---|
| `base_url` | `https://api.datadoghq.com/api/v1` |
| `base_url_env` | `DATADOG_API_URL` |
| Credential | `DD_API_KEY` (header `DD-API-KEY`) and `DD_APP_KEY` (header `DD-APPLICATION-KEY`) |

Assumptions:

- **DD1** (verified, [source](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-api-client-typescript/blob/master/.generator/schemas/v1/openapi.yaml)): Requests carry the API key in `DD-API-KEY` and the application key in `DD-APPLICATION-KEY`; Datadog's clients read them from `DD_API_KEY` and `DD_APP_KEY`. Reading needs the application key too.
- **DD2** (verified, [source](https://docs.datadoghq.com/api/latest/authentication/)): Each Datadog site has its own API host (`https://api.datadoghq.eu`, `https://api.us3.datadoghq.com`, …): outside US1, set `base_url` in the provider block.
- **DD3** (verified, [source](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-api-client-typescript/blob/master/.generator/schemas/v1/openapi.yaml)): `POST /synthetics/tests/api` creates an API test from `name`, `type` (`api`), `config` (`request` with `method` and `url`, `assertions`), `locations`, `options` and `message` (all required), with `subtype` (`http`), `status` (`live` or `paused`) and `tags`, answering it with its `public_id`.
- **DD4** (verified, [source](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-api-client-typescript/blob/master/.generator/schemas/v1/openapi.yaml)): `GET /synthetics/tests/api/{public_id}` answers one API test; `PUT` on the same path replaces its configuration with a whole test definition.
- **DD5** (verified, [source](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-api-client-typescript/blob/master/.generator/schemas/v1/openapi.yaml)): `GET /synthetics/tests` lists every test as `{ tests: [...] }` (`page_size` and `page_number` are optional); `POST /synthetics/tests/delete` with `{ public_ids: [...] }` deletes tests.
- **DD6** **(unverified)**: Without `page_size` the list answers every test of the organisation, and a test name identifies one test (two with one name make `find` refuse with PARAM_INVALID).
- **DD7** **(unverified)**: The fields compared (`config.request`, `config.assertions`, `locations`, `options.tick_every`, `message`, `status`, `tags`) are answered as they were sent, in order.
- **DD8** **(unverified)**: Deleting a test that is already gone answers 404 (destroy treats it as done).
- **DD9** **(unverified)**: Deployment events (`datadog-ci deployment mark`, the DORA deployments API) are not a recipe: they are listed with a POST over a time window and cannot be deleted, so a later run could not find the one it made.

### `datadog.synthetic_api_test`

**Synthetic API test against a preview** (`http.resource`). A Synthetic HTTP test per scope that checks the preview's URL from Datadog's locations, such as `preview pr-42` asserting status 200, with its own monitor. Located by its name; a console edit of its request, assertions, locations, frequency, message, status or tags is drift; destroy deletes the test (and its monitor).

Covers: `datadog-marker` in [the coverage matrix](coverage.md#coverage-matrix). Outputs: `id`. On destroy: deleted (`destroy: keep` on the line leaves it).

| Param | Type | Required | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | — | The test's name; its identity (DD6). |
| `url` | string | yes | — | The URL to request (the preview's URL, or a health path on it). Matches `^https?://\\S+$`. |
| `method` | string | no | `GET` | The HTTP method. One of `GET`, `HEAD`, `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, `DELETE`, `OPTIONS`. |
| `assertions` | list | no | `[{"type":"statusCode","operator":"is","target":200}]` | The assertions, each `{ type, operator, target }` (`statusCode`, `responseTime`, `body`, `header`). |
| `locations` | list | yes | — | The managed locations to run from, such as `aws:us-east-2` or `aws:eu-central-1`. |
| `tick_every` | integer | no | `300` | How often the test runs, in seconds. |
| `message` | string | no | `Preview check managed by Sponson` | The notification message of the test's monitor. |
| `status` | string | no | `live` | `paused` keeps the test without running it. One of `live`, `paused`. |
| `tags` | list | no | `["managed-by:sponson"]` | The test's tags. |

```yaml
# under changes: (no provider block needed)
- id: synthetic_api_test
  adapter: http
  op: resource
  recipe: datadog.synthetic_api_test
  name: preview ${ctx.scope}
  url: https://${ctx.scope}.preview.example.app/api/health
  locations:
    - aws:us-east-2
```

What the line expands into: the [`http.resource`](plan-format.md#httpresource) params, `{ param: <name> }` standing for a param's value and `{<name>}` in a path for its URI-encoded value.

```yaml
find:
  path: /synthetics/tests
  list_path: /tests
  match:
    name: { param: name }
read:
  path: /synthetics/tests/api/{id}
create:
  path: /synthetics/tests/api
  body:
    type: api
    subtype: http
update:
  method: PUT
  body:
    type: api
    subtype: http
delete:
  method: POST
  path: /synthetics/tests/delete
  body:
    public_ids:
      - "{id}"
id_path: /public_id
fields:
  /config/request/method: { param: method }
  /config/request/url: { param: url }
  /config/assertions: { param: assertions }
  locations: { param: locations }
  /options/tick_every: { param: tick_every }
  message: { param: message }
  status: { param: status }
  tags: { param: tags }
```

## Firebase Authentication

Recipe file: [`packages/adapters/recipes/firebase.yaml`](../packages/adapters/recipes/firebase.yaml). Verified on 2026-10-11 against:

- [Identity Toolkit API v2, projects.getConfig](https://docs.cloud.google.com/identity-platform/docs/reference/rest/v2/projects/getConfig)
- [Identity Toolkit API v2, projects.updateConfig](https://docs.cloud.google.com/identity-platform/docs/reference/rest/v2/projects/updateConfig)
- [Identity Toolkit API v2, Config](https://docs.cloud.google.com/identity-platform/docs/reference/rest/v2/Config)
- [Authenticate for using REST](https://docs.cloud.google.com/docs/authentication/rest)

| API default | Value |
|---|---|
| `base_url` | `https://identitytoolkit.googleapis.com/admin/v2` |
| `base_url_env` | `FIREBASE_API_URL` |
| Credential | the token `gcloud auth print-access-token` prints (bearer) |

Assumptions:

- **FB1** (verified, [source](https://docs.cloud.google.com/identity-platform/docs/reference/rest/v2/projects/getConfig)): `GET https://identitytoolkit.googleapis.com/admin/v2/projects/{project}/config` answers the project's Auth `Config`.
- **FB2** (verified, [source](https://docs.cloud.google.com/identity-platform/docs/reference/rest/v2/projects/updateConfig)): `PATCH …/admin/v2/projects/{project}/config?updateMask=authorizedDomains` updates the config with a `Config` body; fields set in the body but not named in `updateMask` are ignored, so the write changes the authorized domains only. It needs one of the `identitytoolkit`, `firebase` or `cloud-platform` OAuth scopes.
- **FB3** (verified, [source](https://docs.cloud.google.com/identity-platform/docs/reference/rest/v2/Config)): `authorizedDomains` is a list of strings, the domains authorized for OAuth redirects; the masked field is replaced by the list sent, so the recipe sends the whole list read just before with one domain added or removed.
- **FB4** (verified, [source](https://docs.cloud.google.com/docs/authentication/rest)): `gcloud auth print-access-token` prints an access token for the signed-in credentials, used as `Authorization: Bearer`. With user credentials some APIs also need the quota project in `x-goog-user-project`: add `headers: { x-goog-user-project: <project> }` to the `providers.http.firebase` block (not needed with a service account; a block's headers are part of its identity).
- **FB5** **(unverified)**: The config has no precondition the update honours (no etag in `Config`): the line locks the project's config (`lockOn`) against other Sponson runs; a console edit made between the read and the write can still be lost.
- **FB6** **(unverified)**: An authorized domain is a host name without scheme, port or path, and is read back exactly as written.
- **FB7** **(unverified)**: The same admin v2 config holds the authorized domains of a Firebase Authentication project with or without the Identity Platform upgrade.

### `firebase.authorized_domain`

**Authorized domain** (`http.list_item`). One domain in Firebase Authentication's authorized domains (Authentication, Settings, Authorized domains), which OAuth sign-in redirects and email links require, such as the preview deployment's host. Read-modify-write of the list with `updateMask=authorizedDomains` under a lock on the project's config; removed on destroy; every other domain (localhost, the Firebase hosting domains) is left as it is.

Covers: `firebase-auth-domains` in [the coverage matrix](coverage.md#coverage-matrix). Outputs: none. On destroy: deleted (`destroy: keep` on the line leaves it).

| Param | Type | Required | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `project` | string | yes | — | The Google Cloud / Firebase project id. |
| `domain` | string | yes | — | The domain, a host name without scheme or path (`pr-42.preview.example.app`, `my-app-git-feat-x.vercel.app`). Matches `^[A-Za-z0-9.-]+$`. |

```yaml
# under changes: (no provider block needed)
- id: authorized_domain
  adapter: http
  op: list_item
  recipe: firebase.authorized_domain
  project: demo-project
  domain: ${ctx.scope}.preview.example.app
```

What the line expands into: the [`http.list_item`](plan-format.md#httplist_item) params, `{ param: <name> }` standing for a param's value and `{<name>}` in a path for its URI-encoded value.

```yaml
parent:
  path: /projects/{project}/config?updateMask=authorizedDomains
  read_path: /projects/{project}/config
list_path: /authorizedDomains
item: { param: domain }
```

## Flagsmith

Recipe file: [`packages/adapters/recipes/flagsmith.yaml`](../packages/adapters/recipes/flagsmith.yaml). Verified on 2026-10-11 against:

- [Admin API authentication](https://docs.flagsmith.com/integrating-with-flagsmith/flagsmith-api-overview/admin-api/authentication)
- [Admin API overview](https://docs.flagsmith.com/integrating-with-flagsmith/flagsmith-api-overview/admin-api)
- [Flagsmith API OpenAPI document](https://api.flagsmith.com/api/v1/swagger.json)

| API default | Value |
|---|---|
| `base_url` | `https://api.flagsmith.com/api/v1` |
| `base_url_env` | `FLAGSMITH_API_URL` |
| Credential | `FLAGSMITH_MASTER_API_KEY` (header `Authorization`, after `Api-Key`) |

Assumptions:

- **FS1** (verified, [source](https://docs.flagsmith.com/integrating-with-flagsmith/flagsmith-api-overview/admin-api/authentication)): The Admin API authenticates with an organisation API key as `Authorization: Api-Key <key>`; Bearer is only for short-lived OIDC-exchanged tokens.
- **FS2** (verified, [source](https://api.flagsmith.com/api/v1/swagger.json)): `POST /environments/` creates an environment from `name` and `project` (both required) and optional `description`, answering it (201) with its integer `id` and its `api_key`, the client-side environment key SDKs use.
- **FS3** (verified, [source](https://api.flagsmith.com/api/v1/swagger.json)): `GET /environments/?project=<id>` lists a project's environments as `{ count, next, previous, results: [...] }`.
- **FS4** (verified, [source](https://api.flagsmith.com/api/v1/swagger.json)): `GET`, `PATCH` and `DELETE /environments/{api_key}/` read, update and delete one environment (DELETE answers 204).
- **FS5** **(unverified)**: A project has fewer environments than one page of the list holds, so `find` sees them all (`next` is a URL, which the http adapter does not follow).
- **FS6** **(unverified)**: A new environment starts with every feature of the project at its default state, and environment names are unique in a project in practice (two with one name make `find` refuse with PARAM_INVALID).
- **FS7** **(unverified)**: `description` is answered as sent; `FLAGSMITH_MASTER_API_KEY` is the variable Flagsmith's Terraform provider reads the key from.
- **FS8** **(unverified)**: Identity and segment overrides are not recipes: Edge projects (Flagsmith SaaS's default) address identities by UUID through `edge-identities`, and a segment override is two objects (a feature segment, then a feature state) created in order.
- **FS9** **(unverified)**: The create takes the project id as a string of digits (`"1234"`) as well as a number, as Django REST Framework's primary-key fields do.

### `flagsmith.environment`

**Environment per preview** (`http.resource`). A Flagsmith environment per scope in a project, such as `preview-pr-42`, starting from the project's default flag states; its client-side environment key is the output `api_key` for the preview's SDK configuration. Located by name in the project; a console edit of its description is drift; destroy deletes the environment with its flag states and identities.

Covers: `flagsmith-override` in [the coverage matrix](coverage.md#coverage-matrix). Outputs: `id`, `api_key`, `environment_id`. On destroy: deleted (`destroy: keep` on the line leaves it).

| Param | Type | Required | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `project_id` | string | yes | — | The project's id, digits as a string (FS9). Matches `^[0-9]+$`. |
| `name` | string | yes | — | The environment's name; its identity in the project (FS6). |
| `description` | string | no | `Preview environment managed by Sponson` | The environment's description. |

```yaml
# under changes: (no provider block needed)
- id: environment
  adapter: http
  op: resource
  recipe: flagsmith.environment
  project_id: "1234"
  name: preview-${ctx.scope}
```

What the line expands into: the [`http.resource`](plan-format.md#httpresource) params, `{ param: <name> }` standing for a param's value and `{<name>}` in a path for its URI-encoded value.
