## Fly.io

Recipe file: [`packages/adapters/recipes/fly.yaml`](../packages/adapters/recipes/fly.yaml). Verified on 2026-10-11 against:

- [Secrets and Fly Apps](https://docs.fly.io/apps/secrets)
- [superfly/fly-go resource_secrets.go (the GraphQL operations flyctl sends)](https://github.com/superfly/fly-go/blob/main/resource_secrets.go)
- [superfly/fly-go schema.graphql](https://github.com/superfly/fly-go/blob/main/schema.graphql)
- [Working with the Machines API (tokens)](https://docs.fly.io/machines/api/working-with-machines-api/)

| API default | Value |
|---|---|
| `base_url` | `https://api.fly.io/graphql` |
| `base_url_env` | `FLY_API_URL` |
| Credential | `FLY_API_TOKEN` (bearer) |

Assumptions:

- **FS1** (verified, [source](https://github.com/superfly/fly-go/blob/main/resource_secrets.go)): `query ($appName: String!) { app(name: $appName) { secrets { name digest createdAt } } }` lists an app's secrets; values are never returned (Fly does not allow reading plain-text secret values), so the recipe locates a secret by name and compares nothing else.
- **FS2** (verified, [source](https://github.com/superfly/fly-go/blob/main/resource_secrets.go)): `mutation($input: SetSecretsInput!) { setSecrets(input: $input) { release { id version } } }` with `{ appId, secrets: [{ key, value }] }` sets secrets; `unsetSecrets(input: { appId, keys })` removes them.
- **FS3** (verified, [source](https://docs.fly.io/apps/secrets)): Plain-text values cannot be read back (`fly secrets list` shows a name, a digest and a date), so a value changed in the console, or in the plan, is not detected: drift is the secret's presence only. To change a value, run `sponson apply --destroy` for the scope (or remove the line, apply, and add it back).
- **FS4** (verified, [source](https://docs.fly.io/apps/secrets)): Machines read secrets as environment variables at boot: a secret set without updating the Machines (as `fly secrets set --stage` does) reaches only Machines started or updated afterwards. Order the line before the PR's `fly deploy`; after a later change run `fly secrets deploy`.
- **FS5** **(unverified)**: A token from `fly tokens create` (`FlyV1 fm2_…`) or `fly auth token` is accepted as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` by the GraphQL API, as the Machines API documents for the same `FLY_API_TOKEN`. (fly-go itself sends a macaroon as `FlyV1 <token>`; a block that needs that sends it with `auth: { header: Authorization, value_env: FLY_API_TOKEN }`.)
- **FS6** **(unverified)**: Unsetting a secret of an app that no longer exists answers an error saying the app could not be found, which the adapter reads as already gone; unsetting an absent key of an existing app is not an error. setSecrets through GraphQL updates no Machines (FS4). Current flyctl sets secrets through the Machines API instead; the GraphQL mutations are not marked deprecated.

### `fly.secret`

**App secret** (`http.resource`). One secret of a Fly app (typically the app made for the pull request, `fly_machines.app`), set with `setSecrets` and removed with `unsetSecrets`. Fly never returns secret values, so only its presence is compared: a secret unset in the console is recreated, a changed value is not noticed (FS3). Machines see it once started or updated after the write: order it before the PR's deploy (FS4).

Covers: `fly-secrets` in [the coverage matrix](coverage.md#coverage-matrix). Outputs: `id`. On destroy: deleted (`destroy: keep` on the line leaves it).

| Param | Type | Required | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `app` | string | yes | — | The app's name. |
| `name` | string | yes | — | The secret's name (the environment variable the Machines see). Matches `^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$`. |
| `value` | string | yes | — | The secret's value, normally a `{ secret }` reference. It is sent, never stored or compared. |

```yaml
# under changes: (no provider block needed)
- id: secret
  adapter: http
  op: resource
  recipe: fly.secret
  app: demo-${ctx.scope}
  name: DATABASE_URL
  value: postgres://app@db.internal:5432/${ctx.scope}
```

What the line expands into: the [`http.resource`](plan-format.md#httpresource) params, `{ param: <name> }` standing for a param's value and `{<name>}` in a path for its URI-encoded value.

```yaml
find:
  graphql:
    query: "query ($appName: String!) { app(name: $appName) { secrets { name digest createdAt } } }"
    variables:
      appName: { param: app }
    data_path: /app/secrets
  match:
    name: { param: name }
create:
  graphql:
    query: "mutation($input: SetSecretsInput!) { setSecrets(input: $input) { release { id version } } }"
    variables:
      input:
        appId: { param: app }
        secrets:
          - key: { param: name }
            value: { param: value }
    idempotent: true
delete:
  graphql:
    query: "mutation($input: UnsetSecretsInput!) { unsetSecrets(input: $input) { release { id version } } }"
    variables:
      input:
        appId: { param: app }
        keys:
          - { param: name }
```

## Fly.io Machines API

Recipe file: [`packages/adapters/recipes/fly_machines.yaml`](../packages/adapters/recipes/fly_machines.yaml). Verified on 2026-10-11 against:

- [Working with the Machines API](https://docs.fly.io/machines/api/working-with-machines-api/)
- [Apps resource](https://docs.fly.io/machines/api/apps-resource/)

| API default | Value |
|---|---|
| `base_url` | `https://api.machines.dev/v1` |
| `base_url_env` | `FLY_MACHINES_API_URL` |
| Credential | `FLY_API_TOKEN` (bearer) |

Assumptions:

- **FM1** (verified, [source](https://docs.fly.io/machines/api/working-with-machines-api/)): The Machines API's public base URL is `https://api.machines.dev`, its paths start with `/v1`, and requests carry `Authorization: Bearer <fly_api_token>`.
- **FM2** (verified, [source](https://docs.fly.io/machines/api/apps-resource/)): `POST /v1/apps` with `app_name` (unique) and `org_slug` (both required) and optional `network` creates an app and answers 201 with `id` and `created_at`.
- **FM3** (verified, [source](https://docs.fly.io/machines/api/apps-resource/)): `GET /v1/apps/{app_name}` answers the app (`id`, `name`, `status`, `organization { name, slug }`), so the name the plan chooses locates it.
- **FM4** (verified, [source](https://docs.fly.io/machines/api/apps-resource/)): `DELETE /v1/apps/{app_name}` answers 202; Machines should be stopped first, and `?force=true` stops them and deletes the app at once, which is what the recipe's destroy sends (a PR app has the PR's Machines running).
- **FM5** **(unverified)**: Deleting the app deletes its secrets and its Machines with it; an app name another organization holds is refused with a conflict, which the adapter then fails to read (403/404) and reports.

### `fly_machines.app`

**App** (`http.resource`). A Fly app per pull request, such as `demo-${ctx.scope}`, in an organization: created with `POST /v1/apps`, located by its name, deleted with its Machines on destroy (`?force=true`). Its secrets are `fly.secret` lines; the Machines are what the PR's `fly deploy` creates. Nothing about the app is compared besides its existence.

Covers: `fly-secrets` in [the coverage matrix](coverage.md#coverage-matrix). Outputs: `id`. On destroy: deleted (`destroy: keep` on the line leaves it).

| Param | Type | Required | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `app_name` | string | yes | — | The app's name, unique across Fly.io. Matches `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$`. |
| `org_slug` | string | yes | — | The organization the app is created in. |
| `network` | string | no | — | A private network (6PN) to put the app on. |

```yaml
# under changes: (no provider block needed)
- id: app
  adapter: http
  op: resource
  recipe: fly_machines.app
  app_name: demo-${ctx.scope}
  org_slug: acme
```

What the line expands into: the [`http.resource`](plan-format.md#httpresource) params, `{ param: <name> }` standing for a param's value and `{<name>}` in a path for its URI-encoded value.

```yaml
read:
  path: /apps/{app_name}
create:
  path: /apps
  body:
    app_name: { param: app_name }
    org_slug: { param: org_slug }
    network: { param: network }
delete:
  path: /apps/{app_name}?force=true
```

## Google Cloud Storage (Firebase Storage)

Recipe file: [`packages/adapters/recipes/gcs.yaml`](../packages/adapters/recipes/gcs.yaml). Verified on 2026-10-11 against:

- [Buckets: patch](https://docs.cloud.google.com/storage/docs/json_api/v1/buckets/patch)
- [Buckets resource (cors)](https://docs.cloud.google.com/storage/docs/json_api/v1/buckets)
- [Set up and view CORS configurations](https://docs.cloud.google.com/storage/docs/using-cors)
- [Performance tips (patch semantics)](https://docs.cloud.google.com/storage/docs/json_api/v1/how-tos/performance)

| API default | Value |
|---|---|
| `base_url` | `https://storage.googleapis.com/storage/v1` |
| `base_url_env` | `GCS_API_URL` |
| Credential | the token `gcloud auth print-access-token` prints (bearer) |

Assumptions:

- **GC1** (verified, [source](https://docs.cloud.google.com/storage/docs/using-cors)): The JSON API takes an OAuth access token as `Authorization: Bearer`; Google's own example gets it from `gcloud auth print-access-token`.
- **GC2** (verified, [source](https://docs.cloud.google.com/storage/docs/using-cors)): `GET /b/{bucket}?fields=cors` answers the bucket's CORS configuration; `PATCH /b/{bucket}?fields=cors` with `{ cors: [...] }` sets it, and `{ cors: [] }` removes it.
- **GC3** (verified, [source](https://docs.cloud.google.com/storage/docs/json_api/v1/how-tos/performance)): A patch that contains a list replaces the whole list: individual entries cannot be added or removed, so the whole `cors` list is written back.
- **GC4** (verified, [source](https://docs.cloud.google.com/storage/docs/json_api/v1/buckets)): Each `cors` entry has `origin` (list), `method` (list), `responseHeader` (list) and `maxAgeSeconds` (integer).
- **GC5** (verified, [source](https://docs.cloud.google.com/storage/docs/json_api/v1/buckets/patch)): `PATCH` takes `ifMetagenerationMatch`, a precondition on the bucket's metageneration. The recipe does not send it (the http adapter has no preconditions); Sponson's own writers are serialised by the parent lock, a writer outside Sponson can still race.
- **GC6** (verified, [source](https://docs.cloud.google.com/storage/docs/json_api/v1/buckets/patch)): Changing a bucket's CORS needs the `storage.buckets.update` permission.
- **GC7** **(unverified)**: A bucket without a CORS configuration answers `{}` (no `cors` field), read as an empty list, and entries are answered as written, in order.
- **GC8** **(unverified)**: An entry is identified by its first origin: the recipe writes one origin per entry, and no other entry of the bucket starts with the same origin.

### `gcs.bucket_cors`

**CORS entry of a bucket** (`http.list_item`). An entry of a bucket's `cors` list allowing one origin, such as the preview's URL on the Firebase Storage bucket `my-app.appspot.com`, with its methods, response headers and max age. The rest of the list is left as it is; a console edit of the entry is drift, and destroy removes only this entry.

Covers: `gcs-cors` in [the coverage matrix](coverage.md#coverage-matrix). Outputs: none. On destroy: deleted (`destroy: keep` on the line leaves it).

| Param | Type | Required | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `bucket` | string | yes | — | The bucket's name (Firebase Storage's default bucket is `<project>.appspot.com` or `<project>.firebasestorage.app`). |
| `origin` | string | yes | — | The origin allowed, without a path (the preview's URL); the entry's identity (GC8). Matches `^(https?://\\S+\|\\*)$`. |
| `methods` | list | no | `["GET","HEAD"]` | The methods allowed. |
| `response_headers` | list | no | `["Content-Type"]` | The response headers the browser may read. |
| `max_age_seconds` | integer | no | `3600` | How long a preflight answer may be cached. |

```yaml
# under changes: (no provider block needed)
- id: bucket_cors
  adapter: http
  op: list_item
  recipe: gcs.bucket_cors
  bucket: my-app.appspot.com
  origin: https://${ctx.scope}.preview.example.app
```

What the line expands into: the [`http.list_item`](plan-format.md#httplist_item) params, `{ param: <name> }` standing for a param's value and `{<name>}` in a path for its URI-encoded value.

```yaml
parent:
  path: /b/{bucket}?fields=cors
  method: PATCH
list_path: /cors
key_field: /origin/0
item:
  origin:
    - { param: origin }
  method: { param: methods }
  responseHeader: { param: response_headers }
  maxAgeSeconds: { param: max_age_seconds }
```

## GitHub

Recipe file: [`packages/adapters/recipes/github.yaml`](../packages/adapters/recipes/github.yaml). Verified on 2026-10-11 against:

- [REST API endpoints for repository webhooks](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/repos/webhooks)
- [Authenticating to the REST API](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/authentication/authenticating-to-the-rest-api)
- [Getting started with the REST API (headers, API versions)](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/using-the-rest-api/getting-started-with-the-rest-api)

| API default | Value |
|---|---|
| `base_url` | `https://api.github.com` |
| `base_url_env` | `GITHUB_API_URL` |
| Credential | `GITHUB_TOKEN` (bearer) |
| `headers` | {"X-GitHub-Api-Version":"2022-11-28","User-Agent":"sponson"} |

Assumptions:

- **GH1** (verified, [source](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/repos/webhooks)): `POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/hooks` creates a repository webhook from `name: web`, `config` (`url`, `content_type`, `secret`, `insecure_ssl`), `events` and `active`, answering 201 with the hook (its integer `id` and `config`), authenticated with `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.
- **GH2** (verified, [source](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/repos/webhooks)): `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/hooks` answers a bare array of hooks, each with `config.url`; it pages with `per_page` (at most 100) and `page`.
- **GH3** (verified, [source](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/repos/webhooks)): `PATCH /repos/{owner}/{repo}/hooks/{hook_id}` updates `config`, `events` (replacing the list) and `active`; a secret set before is removed unless the same or a new one is sent, so every update sends the config's `url` and `secret` again.
- **GH4** (verified, [source](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/repos/webhooks)): `DELETE /repos/{owner}/{repo}/hooks/{hook_id}` answers 204, and 404 when the hook is gone.
- **GH5** (verified, [source](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/repos/webhooks)): Each hook should have a unique config, and hooks may share one only when their events do not overlap. The recipe takes the URL as the hook's identity; two hooks with the same URL make `find` refuse (PARAM_INVALID) instead of guessing.
- **GH6** **(unverified)**: The secret is write-only: answers carry it masked or not at all, so it is sent on create and update but never compared, and a secret changed in the plan reaches GitHub only with the next change of a compared field. Keep it in a secret manager and reference it with `{ secret: … }`.
- **GH7** **(unverified)**: A repository has at most 100 hooks for this purpose (GitHub limits hooks per event), so the first page of `?per_page=100` holds the one `find` looks for.
- **GH8** **(unverified)**: `config.content_type` and `config.insecure_ssl` are answered as sent (`json`/`form`, the strings `"0"`/`"1"`), and `Accept: application/json` is served like `application/vnd.github+json`.
- **GH9** **(unverified)**: The token needs the repository permission Webhooks (write) or the classic `admin:repo_hook` scope; the `GITHUB_TOKEN` of GitHub Actions does not have it, so use a GitHub App token or a fine-grained token. `GITHUB_API_URL` (set by Actions) points at GitHub Enterprise Server where that is the host.

### `github.repo_webhook`

**Repository webhook** (`http.resource`). A repository webhook delivering to an environment's URL, such as the preview deployment's `/api/github` handler. Located by its URL; a console edit of its events, its active flag, its content type or its TLS check is drift. The secret is sent but not compared (GH6).

Covers: `github-webhook` in [the coverage matrix](coverage.md#coverage-matrix). Outputs: `id`. On destroy: deleted (`destroy: keep` on the line leaves it).

| Param | Type | Required | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `owner` | string | yes | — | The repository's owner (user or organization). |
| `repo` | string | yes | — | The repository's name. |
| `url` | string | yes | — | The URL GitHub delivers to; it identifies the hook in the repository. Matches `^https?://\\S+$`. |
| `events` | list | no | `["push"]` | The events that trigger a delivery (`["*"]` for all). |
| `active` | boolean | no | `true` | Whether deliveries are sent. |
| `content_type` | string | no | `json` | The payload's media type. One of `json`, `form`. |
| `insecure_ssl` | string | no | `0` | "1" skips verifying the TLS certificate of the URL. One of `0`, `1`. |
| `secret` | string | no | — | The secret deliveries are signed with (write-only; GH6). Use `{ secret: … }`. |

```yaml
# under changes: (no provider block needed)
- id: repo_webhook
  adapter: http
  op: resource
  recipe: github.repo_webhook
  owner: acme
  repo: app
  url: https://${ctx.scope}.preview.example.com/api/github
```

What the line expands into: the [`http.resource`](plan-format.md#httpresource) params, `{ param: <name> }` standing for a param's value and `{<name>}` in a path for its URI-encoded value.

```yaml
find:
  path: /repos/{owner}/{repo}/hooks?per_page=100
  match:
    /config/url: { param: url }
create:
  path: /repos/{owner}/{repo}/hooks
  body:
    name: web
    config:
      secret: { param: secret }
update:
  method: PATCH
  path: /repos/{owner}/{repo}/hooks/{id}
  body:
    config:
      url: { param: url }
      secret: { param: secret }
delete:
  path: /repos/{owner}/{repo}/hooks/{id}
fields:
  active: { param: active }
  events: { param: events }
  /config/content_type: { param: content_type }
  /config/insecure_ssl: { param: insecure_ssl }
```

## GrowthBook

Recipe file: [`packages/adapters/recipes/growthbook.yaml`](../packages/adapters/recipes/growthbook.yaml). Verified on 2026-10-11 against:

- [REST API reference (authentication, versioning)](https://docs.growthbook.io/api)
- [Get a feature (v2)](https://docs.growthbook.io/api#operation/getFeatureV2)
- [Update a feature (v2)](https://docs.growthbook.io/api#operation/updateFeatureV2)
- [OpenAPI spec](https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/openapi.yaml)

| API default | Value |
|---|---|
| `base_url` | `https://api.growthbook.io/api` |
| `base_url_env` | `GROWTHBOOK_API_URL` |
| Credential | `GROWTHBOOK_API_KEY` (bearer) |

Assumptions:

- **GB1** (verified, [source](https://docs.growthbook.io/api)): GrowthBook Cloud's API is at `https://api.growthbook.io/api` (self-hosted: its API host plus `/api`), authenticated with a secret key or personal access token as `Authorization: Bearer`.
- **GB2** (verified, [source](https://docs.growthbook.io/api#operation/getFeatureV2)): The v1 feature endpoints (rules per environment) are deprecated; in v2 a feature's rules are one top-level `rules` array, each rule naming its `environments` (or `allEnvironments`).
- **GB3** (verified, [source](https://docs.growthbook.io/api#operation/getFeatureV2)): `GET /v2/features/{id}` answers `{ feature: { …, rules: [...] } }`.
- **GB4** (verified, [source](https://docs.growthbook.io/api#operation/updateFeatureV2)): `POST /v2/features/{id}` patch-merges the top-level fields it is sent, and `rules`, when sent, replaces the whole array: so the array is read, the rule added or changed, and the whole array sent back. Rules read with GET may be posted back unchanged. The update publishes a new revision at once.
- **GB5** (verified, [source](https://api.growthbook.io/api/v1/openapi.yaml)): A force rule is `{ type: force, description, condition, value, enabled, allEnvironments, environments }`; `condition` is a JSON query serialised as a string and `value` is a string (`"true"` for a boolean feature).
- **GB6** **(unverified)**: Rule ids may be chosen by the client but what the server does with them is not documented, so the rule is identified by its `description`, which it stores as written; two rules with that description are one rule to Sponson.
- **GB7** **(unverified)**: A rule is read back with `condition` exactly as sent (not reformatted), so the compared fields do not show as changed on every plan.
- **GB8** (verified, [source](https://docs.growthbook.io/api#operation/updateFeatureV2)): When the feature requires approval, the update answers 422 with the gates that blocked it, unless the organisation lets the REST API bypass approvals; the apply then fails.

### `growthbook.force_rule`

**Feature force rule** (`http.list_item`). A force rule on an existing feature that serves a value to the preview in one environment, such as `value "true"` when `{"preview": "pr-42"}`. Added after the feature's other rules (rules are evaluated in order: an earlier rule that matches the preview wins). A console edit of its condition, value, environments or enabled state is drift. Destroy removes the rule.

Covers: `growthbook-force-rule` in [the coverage matrix](coverage.md#coverage-matrix). Outputs: none. On destroy: deleted (`destroy: keep` on the line leaves it).

| Param | Type | Required | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `feature_id` | string | yes | — | The feature's key. |
| `environment` | string | yes | — | The environment the rule applies in. |
| `description` | string | yes | — | The rule's description, unique among the feature's rules; it identifies the rule. |
| `condition` | string | yes | — | The targeting condition, a JSON query as a string. |
| `value` | string | yes | — | The value served, as a string (`"true"` for a boolean feature, JSON for a JSON feature). |
| `enabled` | boolean | no | `true` | Whether the rule is on. |

```yaml
# under changes: (no provider block needed)
- id: force_rule
  adapter: http
  op: list_item
  recipe: growthbook.force_rule
  feature_id: new-checkout
  environment: staging
  description: Sponson preview ${ctx.scope}
  condition: '{"preview": "${ctx.scope}"}'
  value: "true"
```

What the line expands into: the [`http.list_item`](plan-format.md#httplist_item) params, `{ param: <name> }` standing for a param's value and `{<name>}` in a path for its URI-encoded value.

```yaml
parent:
  path: /v2/features/{feature_id}
  method: POST
  item_path: /feature
list_path: /rules
key_field: description
item:
  description: { param: description }
  type: force
  condition: { param: condition }
  value: { param: value }
  enabled: { param: enabled }
  allEnvironments: false
  environments:
    - { param: environment }
```

## Heroku

Recipe file: [`packages/adapters/recipes/heroku.yaml`](../packages/adapters/recipes/heroku.yaml). Verified on 2026-10-11 against:

- [Platform API reference (clients, Config Vars, Review App)](https://devcenter.heroku.com/articles/platform-api-reference)
- [Platform API JSON schema (config-var)](https://api.heroku.com/schema)
- [Configuration and config vars](https://devcenter.heroku.com/articles/config-vars)
- [CLI authentication (HEROKU_API_KEY)](https://devcenter.heroku.com/articles/authentication)

| API default | Value |
|---|---|
| `base_url` | `https://api.heroku.com` |
| `base_url_env` | `HEROKU_API_URL` |
| Credential | `HEROKU_API_KEY` (bearer) |

Assumptions:

- **HK1** (verified, [source](https://devcenter.heroku.com/articles/authentication)): Requests authenticate as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`; the Heroku CLI reads the token from `HEROKU_API_KEY`.
- **HK2** (verified, [source](https://devcenter.heroku.com/articles/platform-api-reference)): Every request must send `Accept: application/vnd.heroku+json; version=3`; without it the API refuses the request (documented as 406 `not_acceptable`; a request without it was answered 400 `missing_version` when checked).
- **HK3** (verified, [source](https://devcenter.heroku.com/articles/platform-api-reference)): `GET /apps/{app_id_or_name}/config-vars` answers the app's config vars as one flat map of name to string value.
- **HK4** (verified, [source](https://devcenter.heroku.com/articles/platform-api-reference)): `PATCH /apps/{app_id_or_name}/config-vars` with a map sets the named vars and removes those set to `null`, leaving every other var as it is: one var is written without reading or rewriting the others, so concurrent writers of other vars cannot lose them (no lock needed).
- **HK5** (verified, [source](https://api.heroku.com/schema)): Config var names match `^\w+$` and values are strings (`null` only as a delete in a PATCH).
- **HK6** (verified, [source](https://devcenter.heroku.com/articles/config-vars)): Every change to config vars creates a new release and restarts the app, so a write takes effect without a separate deploy.
- **HK7** (verified, [source](https://devcenter.heroku.com/articles/platform-api-reference)): Review apps are created asynchronously (`POST /review-apps` answers `pending` with a nullable `app`), by Heroku itself when the pipeline has automatic review apps; this recipe does not create them, it writes vars on an app that exists (the review app's name or id).
- **HK9** **(unverified)**: A PATCH whose `Content-Type` is the same vendor media type (`media_type` sends it as both `Accept` and `Content-Type`) is accepted like `application/json`; the reference's examples send `application/json`.
- **HK8** **(unverified)**: A missing app answers 404 `not_found` on GET and PATCH, which destroy treats as the var being gone.

### `heroku.config_var`

**App config var** (`http.list_item`). One config var on a Heroku app, such as a review app's `API_URL`. Written as a merge patch of that one var (`null` deletes it), so other vars, including other scopes', are never rewritten. A console edit of its value is drift; destroy removes only this var. Heroku restarts the app on every change (HK6).

Covers: `heroku-config-vars` in [the coverage matrix](coverage.md#coverage-matrix). Outputs: none. On destroy: deleted (`destroy: keep` on the line leaves it).

| Param | Type | Required | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `app` | string | yes | — | The app's name or id (a review app's, such as `myapp-pr-42`). |
| `key` | string | yes | — | The config var's name. Matches `^\\w+$`. |
| `value` | string | yes | — | The value: a literal, `{ from }` or `{ secret }`. |

```yaml
# under changes: (no provider block needed)
- id: config_var
  adapter: http
  op: list_item
  recipe: heroku.config_var
  app: myapp-${ctx.scope}
  key: API_URL
  value: https://api-${ctx.scope}.example.com
```

What the line expands into: the [`http.list_item`](plan-format.md#httplist_item) params, `{ param: <name> }` standing for a param's value and `{<name>}` in a path for its URI-encoded value.

```yaml
parent:
  path: /apps/{app}/config-vars
list_path: ""
shape: map
item: { param: key }
value: { param: value }
```

## Honeycomb

Recipe file: [`packages/adapters/recipes/honeycomb.yaml`](../packages/adapters/recipes/honeycomb.yaml). Verified on 2026-10-11 against:

- [Create a Marker](https://docs.honeycomb.io/api/markers/create-a-marker)
- [List All Markers](https://docs.honeycomb.io/api/markers)
- [Update a Marker](https://docs.honeycomb.io/api/markers/update-a-marker)
- [Delete a Marker](https://docs.honeycomb.io/api/markers/delete-a-marker)

| API default | Value |
|---|---|
| `base_url` | `https://api.honeycomb.io` |
| `base_url_env` | `HONEYCOMB_API_URL` |
| Credential | `HONEYCOMB_API_KEY` (header `X-Honeycomb-Team`) |

Assumptions:

- **HC1** (verified, [source](https://docs.honeycomb.io/api/markers/create-a-marker)): `POST /1/markers/{datasetSlug}` creates a marker from `start_time`, `end_time` (Unix seconds), `message`, `type` and `url` (all optional; `start_time` defaults to the request's arrival), answering 201 with the marker and its `id`; `__all__` as the dataset slug makes an environment-wide marker. Requests carry a Configuration Key with the Manage Markers permission in `X-Honeycomb-Team`.
- **HC2** (verified, [source](https://docs.honeycomb.io/api/markers)): `GET /1/markers/{datasetSlug}` answers a bare array of the dataset's markers (`id`, `message`, `type`, `url`, `start_time`, `end_time`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `color`).
- **HC3** (verified, [source](https://docs.honeycomb.io/api/markers/update-a-marker)): `PUT /1/markers/{datasetSlug}/{markerId}` replaces the marker: a field left out of the body is erased.
- **HC4** (verified, [source](https://docs.honeycomb.io/api/markers/delete-a-marker)): `DELETE /1/markers/{datasetSlug}/{markerId}` removes the marker and answers it (200).
- **HC5** (verified, [source](https://docs.honeycomb.io/api/markers/create-a-marker)): The API is served from `api.honeycomb.io` (US) and `api.eu1.honeycomb.io` (EU); EU teams set `base_url` in the provider block.
- **HC6** **(unverified)**: Message and type identify the marker this recipe created among the dataset's markers (Honeycomb does not require them to be unique: two equal ones make `find` refuse with PARAM_INVALID), and the list holds every marker of the dataset in one answer.
- **HC7** **(unverified)**: An update (a changed `url`) re-sends message, type and url but not `start_time`, which Honeycomb then sets to the time of the update (HC3), moving the marker; markers are rarely edited.
- **HC8** **(unverified)**: A deleted marker answers 404 to DELETE, which destroy treats as already gone.

### `honeycomb.marker`

**Deploy marker** (`http.resource`). A marker on an environment's dataset (or on every dataset of the environment with `__all__`) for a deploy, such as `deploy pr-42 0123abc`. Located by its message and type; a console edit of its URL is drift. Destroying the scope removes it; write `destroy: keep` to keep the deploy history.

Covers: `honeycomb-marker` in [the coverage matrix](coverage.md#coverage-matrix). Outputs: `id`. On destroy: deleted (`destroy: keep` on the line leaves it).

| Param | Type | Required | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `dataset` | string | yes | — | The dataset's slug, or `__all__` for an environment-wide marker. |
| `message` | string | yes | — | The marker's text; with its type, its identity (HC6). |
| `type` | string | no | `deploy` | The marker's type, which groups markers (and their color). |
| `url` | string | no | — | The link opened from the marker (the preview or the build). |

```yaml
# under changes: (no provider block needed)
- id: marker
  adapter: http
  op: resource
  recipe: honeycomb.marker
  dataset: __all__
  message: deploy ${ctx.scope} ${ctx.git.sha}
  url: https://${ctx.scope}.preview.example.com
```

What the line expands into: the [`http.resource`](plan-format.md#httpresource) params, `{ param: <name> }` standing for a param's value and `{<name>}` in a path for its URI-encoded value.

```yaml
find:
  path: /1/markers/{dataset}
  match:
    message: { param: message }
    type: { param: type }
create:
  path: /1/markers/{dataset}
update:
  method: PUT
  path: /1/markers/{dataset}/{id}
delete:
  path: /1/markers/{dataset}/{id}
fields:
  url: { param: url }
```

## Inngest

Recipe file: [`packages/adapters/recipes/inngest.yaml`](../packages/adapters/recipes/inngest.yaml). Verified on 2026-10-11 against:

- [Syncing an Inngest app (curl -X PUT on the serve endpoint), Inngest's integration guide](https://www.inngest.com/llm-context.md)
- [Apps in Inngest Cloud (sync methods, when to sync)](https://www.inngest.com/docs/apps/cloud)
- [Environments and branch environments](https://www.inngest.com/docs/platform/environments)
- [The TypeScript SDK's serve handler (InngestCommHandler, PUT = register)](https://github.com/inngest/inngest-js/blob/main/packages/inngest/src/components/InngestCommHandler.ts)
- [REST API v2 OpenAPI document (V2_SyncApp)](https://api-docs.inngest.com/api-specs/v2.json)

No API block: its ops send their request to the app's own URL (a param), with no credential.

Assumptions:

- **IN1** (verified, [source](https://www.inngest.com/llm-context.md)): A `PUT` to the app's serve endpoint (by convention `/api/inngest`, `curl -X PUT https://your-app.com/api/inngest --fail-with-body`) makes the app's SDK register its functions with Inngest; the SDK authenticates that registration with the app's own `INNGEST_SIGNING_KEY`, so the caller sends no credential.
- **IN2** (verified, [source](https://www.inngest.com/docs/platform/environments)): The app registers into the environment its SDK is configured for: `INNGEST_ENV` (or the client's `env` option) names the branch environment and always wins; Vercel's `VERCEL_GIT_COMMIT_REF` is detected automatically, while Netlify, Cloudflare Pages, Railway and Render must pass their branch variable. Sponson does not choose the environment: the app must be configured so.
- **IN3** (verified, [source](https://www.inngest.com/docs/platform/environments)): A branch environment is created on demand the first time an app syncs with it (or events are sent to it), and every branch environment shares one signing key and one event key, so a preview needs no per-branch key.
- **IN4** (verified, [source](https://github.com/inngest/inngest-js/blob/main/packages/inngest/src/components/InngestCommHandler.ts)): Without `x-inngest-sync-kind: in-band` (which this recipe never sends) the serve handler syncs out of band: it calls Inngest's register endpoint itself and answers with that call's status and a JSON body `{ message, modified }`; a failed registration answers 500 (`Failed to register`).
- **IN5** (verified, [source](https://www.inngest.com/docs/apps/cloud)): Sync only once the new version of the code is live: some hosts roll a deploy out over seconds or minutes and an early sync registers the old functions. The recipe's trigger is the deployment's URL (a deploy line's external output, so the line waits for the deploy) and a revision.
- **IN6** (verified, [source](https://www.inngest.com/docs/platform/environments)): Branch environments are archived automatically three days after their latest deployment (archiving stops functions from triggering and keeps the data), and archiving cannot be undone per app; there is no request to undo a sync, so destroy sends nothing and forgets the record.
- **IN7** (verified, [source](https://api-docs.inngest.com/api-specs/v2.json)): The REST API's `POST /v2/apps/{appId}/syncs` (marked beta, `x-beta: true`) takes `{ url }` and answers a sync with `status` pending, success, error or duplicate, but the operation declares no header or parameter that selects a branch environment; this recipe does not use it.
- **IN8** **(unverified)**: Syncing the same deployment again is harmless (the same functions registered again, `modified: false`), so the at-least-once delivery of an action (sent again after a crash before it was recorded) needs no idempotency key.
- **IN9** **(unverified)**: A preview behind Vercel Deployment Protection answers the `PUT` with 401 unless it carries `x-vercel-protection-bypass` with the project's automation bypass secret; pass it with `headers`, as a `{ secret }`.

### `inngest.sync`

**App sync into its branch environment** (`http.action`). Registers a preview deployment's Inngest functions by sending `PUT` to its serve endpoint, once per deployment URL and revision; the app's SDK picks the branch environment (`INNGEST_ENV`, IN2) and signs the registration with its own key (IN1), so no Inngest credential is needed.

Covers: `inngest-sync` in [the coverage matrix](coverage.md#coverage-matrix). Outputs: `modified`. On destroy: nothing is sent (there is nothing to undo); the record is forgotten.

| Param | Type | Required | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `url` | string | yes | — | The deployment's base URL, without a trailing slash: usually `{ from: <deploy line>.preview_url }`, so the sync waits for the deploy (IN5). Matches `^https?://\\S+[^/]$`. |
| `path` | string | no | `/api/inngest` | Where the app serves Inngest's `serve()` handler, appended to `url`. Matches `^/\\S*$`. |
| `revision` | string | yes | — | What else makes it sync again when it changes, usually the commit: `"${ctx.git.sha}"`. |
| `headers` | map | no | — | Extra request headers, such as `x-vercel-protection-bypass: { secret: env://VERCEL_AUTOMATION_BYPASS_SECRET }` for a protected preview (IN9). |

```yaml
# under changes: (no provider block needed)
- id: sync
  adapter: http
  op: action
  recipe: inngest.sync
  url: https://acme-git-feat-x-acme.vercel.app
  revision: ${ctx.git.sha}
```

What the line expands into: the [`http.action`](plan-format.md#httpaction) params, `{ param: <name> }` standing for a param's value, `{ join: [...] }` for its parts joined into one string, and `{<name>}` in a path for its URI-encoded value.

```yaml
trigger:
  url: { param: url }
  path: { param: path }
  revision: { param: revision }
request:
  method: PUT
  url:
    join:
      - { param: url }
      - { param: path }
  headers: { param: headers }
outputs:
  modified: /modified
```

## Kinde

Recipe file: [`packages/adapters/recipes/kinde.yaml`](../packages/adapters/recipes/kinde.yaml). Verified on 2026-10-11 against:

- [Kinde Management API (OpenAPI specification)](https://api-spec.kinde.com/kinde-management-api-spec.yaml)
- [Access the Kinde Management API](https://docs.kinde.com/developer-tools/kinde-api/connect-to-kinde-api/)
- [Kinde Management API JS SDK (conventional variable names)](https://github.com/kinde-oss/management-api-js)

| API default | Value |
|---|---|
| `base_url` | none: set it in the provider block |
| `base_url_env` | `KINDE_API_URL` |
| Credential | `KINDE_MANAGEMENT_CLIENT_ID` / `KINDE_MANAGEMENT_CLIENT_SECRET` (OAuth2 client credentials) |
| Token endpoint | `/oauth2/token` on the origin of `base_url`; override: `KINDE_TOKEN_URL` |
| Audience | `/api` on the origin of `base_url` |

Assumptions:

- **KI1** (verified, [source](https://docs.kinde.com/developer-tools/kinde-api/connect-to-kinde-api/)): A machine-to-machine application authorized for the Management API gets a token from `POST https://<business>.kinde.com/oauth2/token` (form-encoded `grant_type=client_credentials`, `client_id`, `client_secret`, `audience=https://<business>.kinde.com/api`); API calls go to `https://<business>.kinde.com/api/v1/…`. The recipe writes the token URL and audience as paths, so a plan's `base_url: https://<business>.kinde.com/api/v1` names the business once.
- **KI2** (verified, [source](https://api-spec.kinde.com/kinde-management-api-spec.yaml)): `GET /api/v1/applications/{app_id}/auth_redirect_urls` (scope `read:applications_redirect_uris`) answers `{ redirect_urls: [...] }`; `PUT` on the same path (scope `update:applications_redirect_uris`) replaces all of an application's callback URLs with the body's `urls` array. (`POST` adds and `DELETE ?urls=` removes; the recipe replaces the list it read, under a lock, so that one apply is one idempotent write.)
- **KI3** (verified, [source](https://api-spec.kinde.com/kinde-management-api-spec.yaml)): `GET /api/v1/applications/{app_id}/auth_logout_urls` answers `{ logout_urls: [...] }` and `PUT` replaces them with the body's `urls` array, as for callback URLs.
- **KI4** (verified, [source](https://docs.kinde.com/developer-tools/kinde-api/connect-to-kinde-api/)): The audience is always the business's kinde.com subdomain (`https://<business>.kinde.com/api`), even when a custom domain serves sign-in, so `base_url` names the kinde.com subdomain.
- **KI5** (verified, [source](https://github.com/kinde-oss/management-api-js)): `KINDE_MANAGEMENT_CLIENT_ID` and `KINDE_MANAGEMENT_CLIENT_SECRET` are the variables Kinde's Management API SDK reads for the machine-to-machine client.
- **KI6** **(unverified)**: A `PUT` with an empty `urls` list is accepted and leaves the application with no URLs of that kind (destroying the last preview URL of an application that has no others).
- **KI7** **(unverified)**: URLs are read back exactly as written (no normalisation), and the replace has no precondition: the line locks the list (`lockOn`) against other Sponson runs; a console edit made between the read and the write can still be lost.

### `kinde.callback_url`

**Application callback URL** (`http.list_item`). One URL in a Kinde application's Allowed callback URLs, such as the preview's `/api/auth/kinde_callback`. Read-modify-write: the list is read (`redirect_urls`) and replaced (`urls`) with the URL added, under a lock on the list; removed on destroy; every other URL is left as it is.

Covers: `kinde-callbacks` in [the coverage matrix](coverage.md#coverage-matrix). Outputs: none. On destroy: deleted (`destroy: keep` on the line leaves it).

| Param | Type | Required | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `app_id` | string | yes | — | The application's id (its Client ID in the Kinde dashboard). |
| `url` | string | yes | — | The callback URL, exactly as the SDK sends it (`KINDE_REDIRECT_URL` / `KINDE_SITE_URL` + the callback path). Matches `^https?://\\S+$`. |

```yaml
providers:
  http:
    kinde:
      recipe: kinde
      base_url: https://acme.kinde.com/api/v1
changes:
  - id: callback_url
    adapter: http
    op: list_item
    recipe: kinde.callback_url
    app_id: 3b0b5c6c8fcc464fab397f4969b5f482
    url: https://${ctx.scope}.preview.example.app/api/auth/kinde_callback
```

What the line expands into: the [`http.list_item`](plan-format.md#httplist_item) params, `{ param: <name> }` standing for a param's value and `{<name>}` in a path for its URI-encoded value.

```yaml
parent:
  path: /applications/{app_id}/auth_redirect_urls
  method: PUT
  write_list_path: /urls
list_path: /redirect_urls
item: { param: url }
```

### `kinde.logout_url`

**Application allowed logout redirect URL** (`http.list_item`). One URL in a Kinde application's Allowed logout redirect URLs, such as the preview's home page. Read (`logout_urls`) and replaced (`urls`) with the URL added, under a lock on the list; removed on destroy; every other URL is left as it is.

Covers: `kinde-callbacks` in [the coverage matrix](coverage.md#coverage-matrix). Outputs: none. On destroy: deleted (`destroy: keep` on the line leaves it).

| Param | Type | Required | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `app_id` | string | yes | — | The application's id (its Client ID in the Kinde dashboard). |
| `url` | string | yes | — | The URL the SDK redirects to after logout (`KINDE_POST_LOGOUT_REDIRECT_URL`). Matches `^https?://\\S+$`. |

```yaml
providers:
  http:
    kinde:
      recipe: kinde
      base_url: https://acme.kinde.com/api/v1
changes:
  - id: logout_url
    adapter: http
    op: list_item
    recipe: kinde.logout_url
    app_id: 3b0b5c6c8fcc464fab397f4969b5f482
    url: https://${ctx.scope}.preview.example.app
```

What the line expands into: the [`http.list_item`](plan-format.md#httplist_item) params, `{ param: <name> }` standing for a param's value and `{<name>}` in a path for its URI-encoded value.

```yaml
parent:
  path: /applications/{app_id}/auth_logout_urls
  method: PUT
  write_list_path: /urls
list_path: /logout_urls
item: { param: url }
```

## MongoDB Atlas

Recipe file: [`packages/adapters/recipes/mongodb_atlas.yaml`](../packages/adapters/recipes/mongodb_atlas.yaml). Verified on 2026-10-11 against:

- [Atlas Administration API v2 (OpenAPI document)](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/api/doc/atlas-admin-api-v2.json)
- [Create One Database User in One Project](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/api/doc/atlas-admin-api-v2/operation/operation-creategroupdatabaseuser)
- [Configure Atlas API access (API keys use HTTP Digest)](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/configure-api-access/)
- [Atlas CLI environment variables](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/cli/current/atlas-cli-env-variables/)

| API default | Value |
|---|---|
| `base_url` | `https://cloud.mongodb.com/api/atlas/v2` |
| `base_url_env` | `MONGODB_ATLAS_API_URL` |
| Credential | `MONGODB_ATLAS_PUBLIC_API_KEY` / `MONGODB_ATLAS_PRIVATE_API_KEY` (HTTP Digest) |

Assumptions:

- **MA1** (verified, [source](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/configure-api-access/)): Programmatic API keys authenticate with HTTP Digest (the public key as the user name, the private key as the password); service accounts take an OAuth2 client-credentials token instead (`https://cloud.mongodb.com/api/oauth/token`).
- **MA2** (verified, [source](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/cli/current/atlas-cli-env-variables/)): The Atlas CLI keeps the key pair in `MONGODB_ATLAS_PUBLIC_API_KEY` and `MONGODB_ATLAS_PRIVATE_API_KEY`.
- **MA3** (verified, [source](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/api/doc/atlas-admin-api-v2.json)): Requests and answers use the versioned media type `application/vnd.atlas.2023-01-01+json` (in `Accept` and `Content-Type`); the database-user operations are published under that version.
- **MA4** (verified, [source](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/api/doc/atlas-admin-api-v2.json)): `POST /groups/{groupId}/databaseUsers` creates a user from `databaseName`, `groupId`, `roles` and `username` (required), with `password` for SCRAM users (write-only, never answered), optional `scopes` (absent: every cluster of the project) and `deleteAfterDate` (Atlas deletes the user then; within one week of the request). It answers 201 with the user.
- **MA5** (verified, [source](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/api/doc/atlas-admin-api-v2.json)): `GET`, `PATCH` and `DELETE /groups/{groupId}/databaseUsers/{databaseName}/{username}` read, update and delete one user; SCRAM users authenticate against `databaseName` `admin`.
- **MA6** (verified, [source](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/api/doc/atlas-admin-api-v2/operation/operation-creategroupdatabaseuser)): A project supports 100 database users by default (900 at most).
- **MA7** **(unverified)**: A GET of a user that does not exist answers 404; a second create of the same user answers 409.
- **MA8** **(unverified)**: `roles` (each `{ databaseName, roleName, collectionName? }`) and `scopes` (each `{ name, type }`) are answered in the order they were sent, so they compare without drift.
- **MA9** **(unverified)**: `PATCH` takes the user's identifying fields (`databaseName`, `groupId`, `username`) with the changed ones and keeps the password when none is sent.

### `mongodb_atlas.database_user`

**Database user** (`http.resource`). A SCRAM database user per scope on a shared Atlas cluster, such as `app-pr-42` with `readWrite` on the database `app_pr_42`, instead of a cluster per preview. The password is an input: a `{ secret: … }` reference (a value per environment in a secret manager) or a sensitive output of another line, sent on create only and never compared. Located by its user name; a console edit of its roles or scopes is drift; destroy deletes the user (not the database's data).

Covers: `mongodb-atlas-user` in [the coverage matrix](coverage.md#coverage-matrix). Outputs: `id`. On destroy: deleted (`destroy: keep` on the line leaves it).

| Param | Type | Required | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `group_id` | string | yes | — | The project (group) id, 24 hexadecimal digits. Matches `^[0-9a-f]{24}$`. |
| `username` | string | yes | — | The user name, unique in the project; its identity. |
| `password` | string | yes | — | The user's password, as a reference (`{ secret: env://… }`, or `{ from: <line>.<output> }` of a sensitive output); sent on create only (MA4). |
| `roles` | list | yes | — | The roles, each `{ databaseName, roleName }` (`readWrite`, `read`, `dbAdmin`, …). |
| `scopes` | list | no | — | The clusters it may reach, each `{ name, type: CLUSTER }`; absent: every cluster of the project (not compared then). |
| `delete_after` | string | no | — | An ISO 8601 time, within a week, at which Atlas deletes the user by itself (sent on create only). |

```yaml
# under changes: (no provider block needed)
- id: database_user
  adapter: http
  op: resource
  recipe: mongodb_atlas.database_user
  group_id: 32b6e34b3d91647abb20e7b8
  username: app-${ctx.scope}
  password:
    secret: env://PREVIEW_DB_PASSWORD
  roles:
    - databaseName: app_${ctx.scope}
      roleName: readWrite
```

What the line expands into: the [`http.resource`](plan-format.md#httpresource) params, `{ param: <name> }` standing for a param's value and `{<name>}` in a path for its URI-encoded value.

```yaml
read:
  path: /groups/{group_id}/databaseUsers/admin/{username}
create:
  path: /groups/{group_id}/databaseUsers
  body:
    databaseName: admin
    groupId: { param: group_id }
    username: { param: username }
    password: { param: password }
    deleteAfterDate: { param: delete_after }
update:
  method: PATCH
  body:
    databaseName: admin
    groupId: { param: group_id }
    username: { param: username }
id_path: /username
fields:
  roles: { param: roles }
  scopes: { param: scopes }
```

## Okta

Recipe file: [`packages/adapters/recipes/okta.yaml`](../packages/adapters/recipes/okta.yaml). Verified on 2026-10-11 against:

- [Okta Management API (OpenAPI specification, management-minimal.yaml)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/okta/okta-management-openapi-spec/master/dist/current/management-minimal.yaml)
- [Applications API, replace an application](https://developer.okta.com/docs/api/openapi/okta-management/management/tag/Application/#tag/Application/operation/replaceApplication)
- [Trusted Origins API](https://developer.okta.com/docs/api/openapi/okta-management/management/tag/TrustedOrigin/)
- [Okta Terraform provider, configuration (conventional variable names)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/okta/terraform-provider-okta/master/docs/index.md)

| API default | Value |
|---|---|
| `base_url` | none: set it in the provider block |
| `base_url_env` | `OKTA_API_URL` |
| Credential | `OKTA_API_TOKEN` (header `Authorization`, after `SSWS`) |

Assumptions:

- **OK1** (verified, [source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/okta/okta-management-openapi-spec/master/dist/current/management-minimal.yaml)): An API token is sent as `Authorization: SSWS <token>` (the `apiToken` security scheme; Okta recommends scoped OAuth tokens, which need `private_key_jwt` and are not supported here). Every path is under `https://<org>.okta.com/api/v1`.
- **OK2** (verified, [source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/okta/okta-management-openapi-spec/master/dist/current/management-minimal.yaml)): `PUT /api/v1/apps/{appId}` replaces an application: all required properties must be in the body (no partial update), and system-assigned properties (`id`, `name`, `status`, `created`, `lastUpdated`) in the body are ignored. So the recipe sends the whole application read with `GET /api/v1/apps/{appId}` back, with one URI added or removed (`parent.send: parent`).
- **OK3** (verified, [source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/okta/okta-management-openapi-spec/master/dist/current/management-minimal.yaml)): An OIDC application keeps its redirect URIs in `settings.oauthClient.redirect_uris` and its sign-out redirect URIs in `settings.oauthClient.post_logout_redirect_uris`, both arrays of strings.
- **OK4** **(unverified)**: The read-only members of the GET answer that the replace documentation does not list (`_links`, `_embedded`, `credentials.oauthClient.client_id`) are ignored when sent back, as the listed system-assigned ones are.
- **OK5** **(unverified)**: The application replace has no precondition: the line locks the application (`lockOn`, shared by both URI ops) against other Sponson runs; a console edit made between the read and the write can still be lost (the next apply reports it as drift).
- **OK6** (verified, [source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/okta/okta-management-openapi-spec/master/dist/current/management-minimal.yaml)): `POST /api/v1/trustedOrigins` creates a trusted origin from `name`, `origin` and `scopes` (`[{ type: CORS }, { type: REDIRECT }]`, or `IFRAME_EMBED`); `GET /api/v1/trustedOrigins` lists them as a bare array, `q` prefix-matching `name` and `origin`, `limit` up to 200; `PUT /api/v1/trustedOrigins/{id}` replaces one; `DELETE /api/v1/trustedOrigins/{id}` answers 204. `name` and `origin` are each unique.
- **OK7** **(unverified)**: A trusted origin is found among the first 200 that `q=<origin>` matches (pagination follows a `Link` header, which the http adapter does not read); an org with more than 200 origins starting with the same text may not find it and would see the create refused as a duplicate.
- **OK8** **(unverified)**: Scopes are read back as written (`[{ type: CORS }, { type: REDIRECT }]`, no added members), so they can be compared as drift.
- **OK9** (verified, [source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/okta/terraform-provider-okta/master/docs/index.md)): `OKTA_API_TOKEN` is the variable the Okta Terraform provider reads for an API token.

### `okta.redirect_uri`

**OIDC application sign-in redirect URI** (`http.list_item`). One URI in an Okta OIDC application's sign-in redirect URIs (`settings.oauthClient.redirect_uris`), such as the preview's `/login/callback`. The application is read, and written back whole with the URI added (Okta replaces applications only as a whole), under a lock on the application; removed on destroy; every other URI and setting is sent back as read.

Covers: `okta-redirect` in [the coverage matrix](coverage.md#coverage-matrix). Outputs: none. On destroy: deleted (`destroy: keep` on the line leaves it).

| Param | Type | Required | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `app_id` | string | yes | — | The application's id (`0oa…`). |
| `url` | string | yes | — | The redirect URI, exactly as the application sends it as `redirect_uri`. Matches `^\\S+://\\S+$`. |

```yaml
providers:
  http:
    okta:
      recipe: okta
      base_url: https://acme.okta.com/api/v1
changes:
  - id: redirect_uri
    adapter: http
    op: list_item
    recipe: okta.redirect_uri
    app_id: 0oa1gjh63g214q0Hq0g4
    url: https://${ctx.scope}.preview.example.app/login/callback
```

What the line expands into: the [`http.list_item`](plan-format.md#httplist_item) params, `{ param: <name> }` standing for a param's value and `{<name>}` in a path for its URI-encoded value.

```yaml
parent:
  path: /apps/{app_id}
  method: PUT
  send: parent
list_path: /settings/oauthClient/redirect_uris
item: { param: url }
```

### `okta.post_logout_redirect_uri`

**OIDC application sign-out redirect URI** (`http.list_item`). One URI in an Okta OIDC application's sign-out redirect URIs (`settings.oauthClient.post_logout_redirect_uris`), such as the preview's home page. Written back with the whole application, under the application's lock; removed on destroy; every other URI and setting is sent back as read.

Covers: `okta-redirect` in [the coverage matrix](coverage.md#coverage-matrix). Outputs: none. On destroy: deleted (`destroy: keep` on the line leaves it).

| Param | Type | Required | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `app_id` | string | yes | — | The application's id (`0oa…`). |
| `url` | string | yes | — | The URI the application passes as `post_logout_redirect_uri`. Matches `^\\S+://\\S+$`. |

```yaml
providers:
  http:
    okta:
      recipe: okta
      base_url: https://acme.okta.com/api/v1
changes:
  - id: post_logout_redirect_uri
    adapter: http
    op: list_item
    recipe: okta.post_logout_redirect_uri
    app_id: 0oa1gjh63g214q0Hq0g4
    url: https://${ctx.scope}.preview.example.app
```

What the line expands into: the [`http.list_item`](plan-format.md#httplist_item) params, `{ param: <name> }` standing for a param's value and `{<name>}` in a path for its URI-encoded value.

```yaml
parent:
  path: /apps/{app_id}
  method: PUT
  send: parent
list_path: /settings/oauthClient/post_logout_redirect_uris
item: { param: url }
```

### `okta.trusted_origin`

**Trusted origin (CORS and redirect)** (`http.resource`). A trusted origin for the preview, so the Okta Sign-In Widget and Auth JS may call Okta from it (CORS) and Okta may redirect to it after sign-in or sign-out (REDIRECT). Found by its origin; its name and scopes are compared as drift and replaced with `PUT`; deleted on destroy.

Covers: `okta-redirect` in [the coverage matrix](coverage.md#coverage-matrix). Outputs: `id`. On destroy: deleted (`destroy: keep` on the line leaves it).

| Param | Type | Required | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | — | The trusted origin's name, unique in the org. |
| `origin` | string | yes | — | The origin, scheme and host without a path (`https://pr-42.preview.example.app`); unique in the org. Matches `^\\S+://[^/\\s]+$`. |
| `scopes` | list | no | `[{"type":"CORS"},{"type":"REDIRECT"}]` | What the origin is trusted for: `[{ type: CORS }]`, `[{ type: REDIRECT }]`, both (the default), or `IFRAME_EMBED`. |

```yaml
providers:
  http:
    okta:
      recipe: okta
      base_url: https://acme.okta.com/api/v1
changes:
  - id: trusted_origin
    adapter: http
    op: resource
    recipe: okta.trusted_origin
    name: sponson-${ctx.scope}
    origin: https://${ctx.scope}.preview.example.app
```

What the line expands into: the [`http.resource`](plan-format.md#httpresource) params, `{ param: <name> }` standing for a param's value and `{<name>}` in a path for its URI-encoded value.

```yaml
find:
  path: /trustedOrigins?q={origin}&limit=200
  list_path: ""
  match:
    origin: { param: origin }
create:
  path: /trustedOrigins
update:
  method: PUT
  path: /trustedOrigins/{id}
delete:
  path: /trustedOrigins/{id}
item_path: ""
fields:
  name: { param: name }
  origin: { param: origin }
  scopes: { param: scopes }
```

## PostHog

Recipe file: [`packages/adapters/recipes/posthog.yaml`](../packages/adapters/recipes/posthog.yaml). Verified on 2026-10-11 against:

- [Private API (hosts, personal API keys)](https://posthog.com/docs/api)
- [Feature flags API](https://posthog.com/docs/api/feature-flags)
- [OpenAPI schema (FeatureFlag, PersonalAPIKeyAuth)](https://us.posthog.com/api/schema/?format=json)
- [Feature flag serializer (filters validation and merge)](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/blob/master/products/feature_flags/backend/api/feature_flag.py)
- [Feature flag filters schema (condition groups)](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/blob/master/products/feature_flags/backend/api/filters_schema.py)

| API default | Value |
|---|---|
| `base_url` | `https://us.posthog.com` |
| `base_url_env` | `POSTHOG_API_URL` |
| Credential | `POSTHOG_PERSONAL_API_KEY` (bearer) |

Assumptions:

- **PH1** (verified, [source](https://posthog.com/docs/api)): The private API is at `https://us.posthog.com` (US cloud) or `https://eu.posthog.com` (EU cloud; set `base_url`), authenticated with a personal API key as `Authorization: Bearer`, with the `feature_flag:read` and `feature_flag:write` scopes.
- **PH2** (verified, [source](https://us.posthog.com/api/schema/?format=json)): `GET /api/projects/{project_id}/feature_flags/{id}/` (trailing slash) answers the flag bare, with its release conditions in `filters.groups`; `PATCH` on the same path updates it and answers it bare.
- **PH3** (verified, [source](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/blob/master/products/feature_flags/backend/api/filters_schema.py)): A condition group is `{ properties: [{ key, type, operator, value }], rollout_percentage, variant }`; `exact` takes a list of values. Groups have no id, so the group is identified by the first value of its first property (the preview host).
- **PH4** (verified, [source](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/blob/master/products/feature_flags/backend/api/feature_flag.py)): A PATCH of `filters` merges top-level keys into the stored filters (`{**stored_filters, **filters}`): sending `{ filters: { groups } }` replaces the groups and keeps `multivariate`, `payloads` and the rest. This is in the serializer's source, not the docs.
- **PH5** **(unverified)**: Self-hosted or older PostHog versions merge `filters` the same way (the merge arrived with 2026's validation work). On a version that replaces `filters` whole, every write would drop the flag's variants and payloads: check before pointing the recipe at one.
- **PH6** **(unverified)**: A group is read back as written (the serializer drops unknown keys and adds none to the declared ones), so the compared `properties`, `rollout_percentage` and `variant` do not show as changed on every plan.
- **PH7** (verified, [source](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/blob/master/products/approvals/backend/decorators.py)): A flag under an approval policy answers a PATCH with 409 (`approval_required` or `change_request_pending`); the apply then fails with PROVIDER_CONFLICT rather than waiting for the approval.

### `posthog.release_condition`

**Flag release condition** (`http.list_item`). A release condition (condition group) on an existing feature flag that matches the preview, such as `$host exact [pr-42.preview.example.com]` at 100%. Groups are OR'd; the flag's other groups, variants and payloads are left as they are. A console edit of its properties, rollout or variant is drift. Destroy removes the group (with the last group gone, the flag matches no one).

Covers: `posthog-release-condition` in [the coverage matrix](coverage.md#coverage-matrix). Outputs: none. On destroy: deleted (`destroy: keep` on the line leaves it).

| Param | Type | Required | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `project_id` | string | yes | — | The project's numeric id (Project settings). Matches `^[0-9]+$`. |
| `flag_id` | string | yes | — | The flag's numeric id (in the flag's URL), not its key. Matches `^[0-9]+$`. |
| `property` | string | yes | — | The property the condition tests. It must be known when the flag is evaluated (a person property, or one passed with the evaluation). |
| `property_type` | string | no | `person` | Whether `property` is a person or a group property. One of `person`, `group`. |
| `operator` | string | no | `exact` | How the property is compared with `value`. One of `exact`, `is_not`, `icontains`, `regex`. |
| `value` | string | yes | — | The value that matches the preview (such as its host); it identifies the condition on the flag. |
| `rollout_percentage` | integer | no | `100` | The share of matching users the flag is on for (0–100). |
| `variant` | string | no | — | For a multivariate flag, the variant the condition serves. |

```yaml
# under changes: (no provider block needed)
- id: release_condition
  adapter: http
  op: list_item
  recipe: posthog.release_condition
  project_id: "12345"
  flag_id: "678"
  property: $host
  value: ${ctx.scope}.preview.example.com
```

What the line expands into: the [`http.list_item`](plan-format.md#httplist_item) params, `{ param: <name> }` standing for a param's value and `{<name>}` in a path for its URI-encoded value.

```yaml
parent:
  path: /api/projects/{project_id}/feature_flags/{flag_id}/
  method: PATCH
list_path: /filters/groups
key_field: /properties/0/value/0
item:
  properties:
    - key: { param: property }
      type: { param: property_type }
      operator: { param: operator }
      value:
        - { param: value }
  rollout_percentage: { param: rollout_percentage }
  variant: { param: variant }
```

## Postmark (Account API)

Recipe file: [`packages/adapters/recipes/postmark.yaml`](../packages/adapters/recipes/postmark.yaml). Verified on 2026-10-11 against:

- [Servers API](https://postmarkapp.com/developer/api/servers-api)
- [API overview (authentication)](https://postmarkapp.com/developer/api/overview)

| API default | Value |
|---|---|
| `base_url` | `https://api.postmarkapp.com` |
| `base_url_env` | `POSTMARK_API_URL` |
| Credential | `POSTMARK_ACCOUNT_TOKEN` (header `X-Postmark-Account-Token`) |

Assumptions:

- **PM1** (verified, [source](https://postmarkapp.com/developer/api/servers-api)): The Servers API authenticates with the account token in `X-Postmark-Account-Token` (account owner only) and takes and answers JSON.
- **PM2** (verified, [source](https://postmarkapp.com/developer/api/servers-api)): `POST /servers` creates a server from `Name` (required), `Color`, `DeliveryType` (`Live` or `Sandbox`, fixed after creation), `InboundHookUrl`, `TrackOpens`, `TrackLinks` and more, answering the server with its integer `ID`, its settings and `ApiTokens` (the server's tokens).
- **PM3** (verified, [source](https://postmarkapp.com/developer/api/servers-api)): `GET /servers?count=&offset=&name=` answers `{ TotalCount, Servers: [...] }`; `name` is a substring search (`MyServer` also matches `MyServer Production`), so the recipe matches the exact `Name` among the results.
- **PM4** (verified, [source](https://postmarkapp.com/developer/api/servers-api)): `PUT /servers/{serverid}` changes the settings sent (everything but `DeliveryType`); `GET /servers/{serverid}` answers the server with its `ApiTokens`, so the server token stays readable.
- **PM5** (verified, [source](https://postmarkapp.com/developer/api/servers-api)): `DELETE /servers/{serverid}` removes a server, but is not enabled for every account: where Postmark support has not enabled it, destroy fails and the line needs `destroy: keep`.
- **PM6** **(unverified)**: Server names are unique in the account (a second create with the same name is refused), and an account has fewer than 500 servers, so the first page of `count=500` holds the one `find` looks for.
- **PM7** **(unverified)**: `Color`, `TrackOpens`, `TrackLinks` and `InboundHookUrl` are answered as sent (`InboundHookUrl` empty when unset), so they compare without drift.

### `postmark.server`

**Server** (`http.resource`). A Postmark server per environment, such as `sponson-preview-pr-42`, with its inbound webhook URL and tracking settings. Its token is a sensitive output for the app's environment (`{ from: <line>.server_token }`). Located by its name; a console edit of its color, tracking or inbound hook URL is drift. Its webhooks: `postmark_server.webhook` with `credential: { from: <this line>.server_token }`.

Covers: `postmark-server-webhook` in [the coverage matrix](coverage.md#coverage-matrix). Outputs: `id`, `server_token` (sensitive). On destroy: deleted (`destroy: keep` on the line leaves it).

| Param | Type | Required | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | — | The server's name, unique in the account (PM6); its identity. |
| `color` | string | no | `Blue` | The server's color in the Postmark dashboard. One of `Purple`, `Blue`, `Turquoise`, `Green`, `Red`, `Yellow`, `Grey`, `Orange`. |
| `delivery_type` | string | no | `Sandbox` | `Sandbox` accepts mail without delivering it; fixed once the server exists (sent on create only). One of `Live`, `Sandbox`. |
| `inbound_hook_url` | string | no | `` | The URL inbound mail is posted to (empty for none). |
| `track_opens` | boolean | no | `false` | Track opens of outbound mail. |
| `track_links` | string | no | `None` | Track link clicks of outbound mail. One of `None`, `HtmlAndText`, `HtmlOnly`, `TextOnly`. |

```yaml
# under changes: (no provider block needed)
- id: server
  adapter: http
  op: resource
  recipe: postmark.server
  name: sponson-${ctx.env}-${ctx.scope}
  inbound_hook_url: https://${ctx.scope}.preview.example.com/api/postmark/inbound
```

What the line expands into: the [`http.resource`](plan-format.md#httpresource) params, `{ param: <name> }` standing for a param's value and `{<name>}` in a path for its URI-encoded value.

```yaml
find:
  path: /servers?count=500&offset=0&name={name}
  list_path: /Servers
  match:
    Name: { param: name }
create:
  path: /servers
  body:
    DeliveryType: { param: delivery_type }
update:
  method: PUT
  path: /servers/{id}
delete:
  path: /servers/{id}
id_path: /ID
fields:
  Color: { param: color }
  InboundHookUrl: { param: inbound_hook_url }
  TrackOpens: { param: track_opens }
  TrackLinks: { param: track_links }
outputs:
  server_token:
    path: /ApiTokens/0
    sensitive: true
```

## Postmark (Server API)

Recipe file: [`packages/adapters/recipes/postmark_server.yaml`](../packages/adapters/recipes/postmark_server.yaml). Verified on 2026-10-11 against:

- [Webhooks API](https://postmarkapp.com/developer/api/webhooks-api)
- [API overview (authentication)](https://postmarkapp.com/developer/api/overview)

| API default | Value |
|---|---|
| `base_url` | `https://api.postmarkapp.com` |
| `base_url_env` | `POSTMARK_API_URL` |
| Credential | `POSTMARK_SERVER_TOKEN` (header `X-Postmark-Server-Token`) |

Assumptions:

- **PS1** (verified, [source](https://postmarkapp.com/developer/api/webhooks-api)): The Webhooks API authenticates with a server's token in `X-Postmark-Server-Token`, so it manages the webhooks of that one server.
- **PS2** (verified, [source](https://postmarkapp.com/developer/api/webhooks-api)): `POST /webhooks` creates a webhook from `Url` (required), `MessageStream` (default `outbound`), `HttpAuth`, `HttpHeaders` and `Triggers` (`Open { Enabled, PostFirstOpenOnly }`, `Click`, `Delivery`, `Bounce { Enabled, IncludeContent }`, `SpamComplaint { Enabled, IncludeContent }`, `SubscriptionChange`, each with `Enabled`), answering the webhook with its integer `ID`.
- **PS3** (verified, [source](https://postmarkapp.com/developer/api/webhooks-api)): `GET /webhooks` (optionally `?MessageStream=`) answers `{ Webhooks: [...] }` with each webhook's `ID`, `Url`, `MessageStream` and `Triggers`.
- **PS4** (verified, [source](https://postmarkapp.com/developer/api/webhooks-api)): `PUT /webhooks/{Id}` changes `Url`, `HttpAuth`, `HttpHeaders` and `Triggers` (not `MessageStream`), re-verifying the endpoint when the URL or the triggers change; `DELETE /webhooks/{Id}` removes it.
- **PS5** (verified, [source](https://postmarkapp.com/developer/api/webhooks-api)): Postmark tests the endpoint when a webhook is created; `Verify: false` saves it without the test (a preview that is not deployed yet would fail it).
- **PS6** **(unverified)**: A URL identifies one webhook of the server (two webhooks with the same URL, on different streams, make `find` refuse with PARAM_INVALID), and every trigger's `Enabled` is answered as a boolean even when it was not sent.
- **PS7** **(unverified)**: `PostFirstOpenOnly` and `IncludeContent` are left at Postmark's defaults; only which events are delivered is compared.
- **PS8** **(unverified)**: A server's webhooks belong to it: deleting the server (`DELETE /servers/{id}`, Account API) removes them, so a webhook line authenticated with the server's own token can leave its destroy to the server's line.

### `postmark_server.webhook`

**Webhook of a server** (`http.resource`). A webhook of one Postmark server delivering to an environment's URL, such as the preview's `/api/postmark` handler, with the events it enables. Located by its URL; a console edit of an event's `Enabled` is drift. The server is the one whose token is in `POSTMARK_SERVER_TOKEN` (a shared staging server), or, for a server the same plan creates per environment (`postmark.server`), the line says `credential: { from: <server line>.server_token }` and `destroy: keep`: deleting the server removes its webhooks (PS8).

Covers: `postmark-server-webhook` in [the coverage matrix](coverage.md#coverage-matrix). Outputs: `id`. On destroy: deleted (`destroy: keep` on the line leaves it).

| Param | Type | Required | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `url` | string | yes | — | The URL events are posted to; its identity (PS6). Matches `^https?://\\S+$`. |
| `message_stream` | string | no | `outbound` | The message stream whose events are delivered (sent on create only). |
| `verify` | boolean | no | `false` | Have Postmark test the URL when the webhook is created (PS5). |
| `delivery` | boolean | no | `true` | Deliver `Delivery` events. |
| `bounce` | boolean | no | `true` | Deliver `Bounce` events. |
| `spam_complaint` | boolean | no | `true` | Deliver `SpamComplaint` events. |
| `open` | boolean | no | `false` | Deliver `Open` events. |
| `click` | boolean | no | `false` | Deliver `Click` events. |
| `subscription_change` | boolean | no | `false` | Deliver `SubscriptionChange` events. |

```yaml
# under changes: (no provider block needed)
- id: webhook
  adapter: http
  op: resource
  recipe: postmark_server.webhook
  url: https://${ctx.scope}.preview.example.com/api/postmark
```

What the line expands into: the [`http.resource`](plan-format.md#httpresource) params, `{ param: <name> }` standing for a param's value and `{<name>}` in a path for its URI-encoded value.

```yaml
find:
  path: /webhooks
  list_path: /Webhooks
  match:
    Url: { param: url }
create:
  path: /webhooks
  body:
    MessageStream: { param: message_stream }
    Verify: { param: verify }
update:
  method: PUT
  path: /webhooks/{id}
delete:
  path: /webhooks/{id}
id_path: /ID
fields:
  /Triggers/Delivery/Enabled: { param: delivery }
  /Triggers/Bounce/Enabled: { param: bounce }
  /Triggers/SpamComplaint/Enabled: { param: spam_complaint }
  /Triggers/Open/Enabled: { param: open }
  /Triggers/Click/Enabled: { param: click }
  /Triggers/SubscriptionChange/Enabled: { param: subscription_change }
```

## Prisma Postgres

Recipe file: [`packages/adapters/recipes/prisma.yaml`](../packages/adapters/recipes/prisma.yaml). Verified on 2026-10-11 against:

- [Management API OpenAPI document](https://api.prisma.io/v1/doc)
- [Management API guide (base URL, service tokens)](https://www.prisma.io/docs/guides/management-api-basic)
- [Connecting to your database (connection strings)](https://www.prisma.io/docs/postgres/database/connecting-to-your-database)

| API default | Value |
|---|---|
| `base_url` | `https://api.prisma.io/v1` |
| `base_url_env` | `PRISMA_API_URL` |
| Credential | `PRISMA_SERVICE_TOKEN` (bearer) |

Assumptions:

- **PP1** (verified, [source](https://www.prisma.io/docs/guides/management-api-basic)): The Management API at `https://api.prisma.io/v1` authenticates with a workspace service token as `Authorization: Bearer`; Prisma's guide keeps it in `PRISMA_SERVICE_TOKEN`.
- **PP2** (verified, [source](https://api.prisma.io/v1/doc)): Answers are enveloped: one object as `{ data: {…} }`, a list as `{ data: [...], pagination: { nextCursor, hasMore } }`, paged with `?cursor=`.
- **PP3** (verified, [source](https://api.prisma.io/v1/doc)): `POST /v1/projects/{projectId}/databases` with `{ name, region, source? }` creates a database (201); `source: { type: database, databaseId }` copies an existing one. It answers the database with `id`, `name`, `status` (`provisioning` or `ready`) and `connections[]`.
- **PP4** (verified, [source](https://api.prisma.io/v1/doc)): `GET /v1/projects/{projectId}/databases` lists the project's databases with `id` and `name`; it has no name filter, so the list is searched page by page.
- **PP5** **(unverified)**: Database names are not unique (the project-scoped create documents no 409), so two databases with one name make `find.match` ambiguous, which is refused with PARAM_INVALID rather than guessed. Sponson never creates a second one: it looks the name up before every create.
- **PP6** (verified, [source](https://api.prisma.io/v1/doc)): `GET /v1/databases/{databaseId}` answers the database (404 when it does not exist); `DELETE` on the same path deletes it (204; 404 when gone; 403 for a project's default database).
- **PP7** **(unverified)**: The connection strings (`connections[0].endpoints.direct.connectionString`, and `.pooled` when there is a pooled endpoint) are in the create answer only: list and get answer the endpoints' host and port without them. So they are once-only outputs (ADR 0018), and a create whose answer was lost leaves dependents to be refused until the database is recreated. Inferred from the schemas; not stated in the docs.
- **PP8** **(unverified)**: `connections[0]` is the database's default connection, present in every create answer.
- **PP9** **(unverified)**: A database answered with `status: provisioning` accepts connections within seconds; nothing waits for `ready` (the API has no readiness the http adapter can poll), so a dependent deployment that starts at once may see connection errors for that long.
- **PP10** (verified, [source](https://www.prisma.io/docs/postgres/database/connecting-to-your-database)): Connection strings have the form `postgres://USER:PASSWORD@db.prisma.io:5432/?sslmode=require` (direct) and `postgres://USER:PASSWORD@pooled.db.prisma.io:5432/?sslmode=require` (pooled).

### `prisma.database`

**Database** (`http.resource`). An empty Postgres database per scope in a Prisma Postgres project, such as `app-pr-42`. Its connection strings exist only in the create answer, so they are once-only outputs: reference them from the line that needs them (an env var) in the same plan. Located by name; only its existence is compared for drift; destroy deletes it and its data.

Covers: `prisma-postgres-database` in [the coverage matrix](coverage.md#coverage-matrix). Outputs: `id`, `status`, `direct_url` (sensitive, [once](plan-format.md#once-only-outputs): only from the create), `pooled_url` (sensitive, [once](plan-format.md#once-only-outputs): only from the create). On destroy: deleted (`destroy: keep` on the line leaves it).

| Param | Type | Required | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `project_id` | string | yes | — | The project's id. |
| `name` | string | yes | — | The database's name. |
| `region` | string | no | `us-east-1` | Where it runs. One of `us-east-1`, `us-west-1`, `eu-west-3`, `eu-central-1`, `ap-northeast-1`, `ap-southeast-1`. |

```yaml
# under changes: (no provider block needed)
- id: database
  adapter: http
  op: resource
  recipe: prisma.database
  project_id: proj_cm1a2b3c4d5e6f7g8h9
  name: app-${ctx.scope}
```

What the line expands into: the [`http.resource`](plan-format.md#httpresource) params, `{ param: <name> }` standing for a param's value and `{<name>}` in a path for its URI-encoded value.

```yaml
find:
  path: /projects/{project_id}/databases
  list_path: /data
  next: /pagination/nextCursor
  match:
    name: { param: name }
read:
  path: /databases/{id}
create:
  path: /projects/{project_id}/databases
  body:
    region: { param: region }
item_path: /data
outputs:
  status: /status
  direct_url:
    path: /connections/0/endpoints/direct/connectionString
    sensitive: true
    once: true
  pooled_url:
    path: /connections/0/endpoints/pooled/connectionString
    sensitive: true
    once: true
```

### `prisma.database_copy`

**Database copied from another** (`http.resource`). A Postgres database per scope copied from an existing one (`source: { type: database }`), such as `app-pr-42` with the data of `app`. Otherwise like `prisma.database`: once-only connection strings, existence-only drift, destroy deletes the copy (never the source).

Covers: `prisma-postgres-database` in [the coverage matrix](coverage.md#coverage-matrix). Outputs: `id`, `status`, `direct_url` (sensitive, [once](plan-format.md#once-only-outputs): only from the create), `pooled_url` (sensitive, [once](plan-format.md#once-only-outputs): only from the create). On destroy: deleted (`destroy: keep` on the line leaves it).

| Param | Type | Required | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `project_id` | string | yes | — | The project's id. |
| `name` | string | yes | — | The new database's name. |
| `source_database_id` | string | yes | — | The id of the database to copy. |
