## Upstash QStash

Recipe file: [`packages/adapters/recipes/qstash.yaml`](../packages/adapters/recipes/qstash.yaml). Verified on 2026-10-11 against:

- [Authentication](https://upstash.com/docs/qstash/api/authentication)
- [Create a schedule](https://upstash.com/docs/qstash/api-reference/schedules/create-a-schedule)
- [Get a schedule](https://upstash.com/docs/qstash/api-reference/schedules/get-a-schedule)
- [Delete a schedule](https://upstash.com/docs/qstash/api-reference/schedules/delete-a-schedule)
- [API examples (raw destination URL in the path)](https://upstash.com/docs/qstash/overall/apiexamples)
- [Multi-region (base URLs, tokens)](https://upstash.com/docs/qstash/howto/multi-region)

| API default | Value |
|---|---|
| `base_url` | `https://qstash.upstash.io` |
| `base_url_env` | `QSTASH_API_URL` |
| Credential | `QSTASH_TOKEN` (bearer) |

Assumptions:

- **QS1** (verified, [source](https://upstash.com/docs/qstash/api/authentication)): Requests authenticate with the QStash token as `Authorization: Bearer`; the SDKs read it from `QSTASH_TOKEN`.
- **QS2** (verified, [source](https://upstash.com/docs/qstash/howto/multi-region)): Each region (`qstash.upstash.io` = EU, `qstash-us-east-1.upstash.io`) has its own token and its own schedules; the default here is the EU URL, and a US account overrides `base_url` in its block.
- **QS3** (verified, [source](https://upstash.com/docs/qstash/api-reference/schedules/create-a-schedule)): `POST /v2/schedules/{destination}` creates a schedule: the cron in `Upstash-Cron`, the method used to call the destination in `Upstash-Method` (default POST), the request body as the message delivered on every run. It answers `{ scheduleId }`.
- **QS4** (verified, [source](https://upstash.com/docs/qstash/api-reference/schedules/create-a-schedule)): With `Upstash-Schedule-Id`, a schedule with that id is updated with the new settings if it exists (an upsert): the id is the client's, the read path names it, and the same request is both create and update.
- **QS5** (verified, [source](https://upstash.com/docs/qstash/overall/apiexamples)): The official example writes the destination URL in the path as it is (`/v2/schedules/https://example.com`), hence the `{+destination}` placeholder.
- **QS6** **(unverified)**: A destination URL with a query string arrives intact with its `?` escaped as `%3F` (a raw `?` would end the path); not documented.
- **QS7** (verified, [source](https://upstash.com/docs/qstash/api-reference/schedules/get-a-schedule)): `GET /v2/schedules/{scheduleId}` answers the schedule bare with `scheduleId`, `cron`, `destination`, `method` and `body`, and 404 when there is none; `DELETE` on the same path removes it.
- **QS8** **(unverified)**: Deleting a schedule that is already gone answers 404 (only 200 is documented), which destroy treats as done.
- **QS9** (verified, [source](https://upstash.com/docs/qstash/api-reference/schedules/create-a-schedule)): Schedule ids are alphanumerics, hyphens, periods and underscores (400 otherwise); a cron may carry a `CRON_TZ=<zone>` prefix and runs at most once a minute.
- **QS10** **(unverified)**: `GET` returns `cron`, `destination` and `method` exactly as they were sent (the cron string unnormalised), so comparing them is not drift on every plan.

### `qstash.schedule`

**Schedule** (`http.resource`). A cron schedule that calls a preview's URL, such as `/api/cron` of `pr-42`, under a schedule id per scope. Created and updated by the same upsert (QS4); a console edit of its cron, destination or method is drift; destroy deletes it. The message body is sent on create and update but not compared.

Covers: `qstash-schedule` in [the coverage matrix](coverage.md#coverage-matrix). Outputs: `id`. On destroy: deleted (`destroy: keep` on the line leaves it).

| Param | Type | Required | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `schedule_id` | string | yes | — | The schedule's id, chosen by the plan (one per scope). Matches `^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$`. |
| `destination` | string | yes | — | The URL the schedule calls. Matches `^https?://`. |
| `cron` | string | yes | — | The cron expression, optionally prefixed `CRON_TZ=<zone> `. |
| `method` | string | no | `POST` | The HTTP method used to call the destination. One of `GET`, `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, `DELETE`. |
| `body` | map | no | — | The JSON message delivered on every run (sent, not compared). |

```yaml
# under changes: (no provider block needed)
- id: schedule
  adapter: http
  op: resource
  recipe: qstash.schedule
  schedule_id: cron-${ctx.scope}
  destination: https://${ctx.scope}.preview.example.com/api/cron
  cron: "*/15 * * * *"
```

What the line expands into: the [`http.resource`](plan-format.md#httpresource) params, `{ param: <name> }` standing for a param's value and `{<name>}` in a path for its URI-encoded value.

```yaml
read:
  path: /v2/schedules/{schedule_id}
create:
  path: /v2/schedules/{+destination}
  headers:
    Upstash-Schedule-Id: { param: schedule_id }
    Upstash-Cron: { param: cron }
    Upstash-Method: { param: method }
  send_fields: false
  body: { param: body }
update:
  method: POST
  path: /v2/schedules/{+destination}
  headers:
    Upstash-Schedule-Id: { param: schedule_id }
    Upstash-Cron: { param: cron }
    Upstash-Method: { param: method }
  send_fields: false
  body: { param: body }
id_path: /scheduleId
fields:
  cron: { param: cron }
  destination: { param: destination }
  method: { param: method }
```

## Railway

Recipe file: [`packages/adapters/recipes/railway.yaml`](../packages/adapters/recipes/railway.yaml). Verified on 2026-10-11 against:

- [Public API (endpoint, tokens, errors)](https://docs.railway.com/reference/public-api)
- [Manage Variables with the Public API](https://docs.railway.com/guides/manage-variables)
- [Environments (PR environments)](https://docs.railway.com/reference/environments)
- [CLI (RAILWAY_TOKEN and RAILWAY_API_TOKEN)](https://docs.railway.com/guides/cli)
- [railwayapp/cli GraphQL schema](https://github.com/railwayapp/cli/blob/master/src/gql/schema.json)

| API default | Value |
|---|---|
| `base_url` | `https://backboard.railway.com/graphql/v2` |
| `base_url_env` | `RAILWAY_API_URL` |
| Credential | `RAILWAY_API_TOKEN` (bearer) |

Assumptions:

- **RY1** (verified, [source](https://docs.railway.com/reference/public-api)): The public API is one GraphQL endpoint, `https://backboard.railway.com/graphql/v2`; account, workspace and OAuth tokens are sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`, project tokens in `Project-Access-Token` instead (a project token therefore needs a hand-written block with `auth: { header: Project-Access-Token, value_env: RAILWAY_TOKEN }`).
- **RY2** (verified, [source](https://docs.railway.com/guides/cli)): The Railway CLI reads an account or workspace token from `RAILWAY_API_TOKEN` and a project token from `RAILWAY_TOKEN`, so the bearer credential of this recipe is `RAILWAY_API_TOKEN`.
- **RY3** (verified, [source](https://docs.railway.com/reference/public-api)): Failures may be HTTP 200 with an `errors` array (a denied query among them); 400 is a parse or validation failure, 429 a rate limit with `Retry-After`. Queries are safe to retry; a mutation only when no answer arrived.
- **RY4** (verified, [source](https://docs.railway.com/guides/manage-variables)): `variables(projectId, environmentId, serviceId?, unrendered?)` answers the variables of a service in an environment (without `serviceId`, the environment's shared variables) as a map of name to value; `unrendered: true` answers references such as `${{Postgres.DATABASE_URL}}` as written instead of resolved, so a value is compared as it was set.
- **RY5** (verified, [source](https://docs.railway.com/guides/manage-variables)): `variableUpsert(input: { projectId, environmentId, serviceId?, name, value, skipDeploys? })` creates or replaces one variable (without `serviceId`, a shared variable); by default it triggers a redeploy of the service (`skipDeploys` defaults to false).
- **RY6** (verified, [source](https://docs.railway.com/guides/manage-variables)): `variableDelete(input: { projectId, environmentId, serviceId?, name })` deletes one variable.
- **RY7** (verified, [source](https://docs.railway.com/reference/environments)): Railway creates a PR environment when a pull request is opened (with PR environments enabled) and deletes it, with its variables, when the pull request is merged or closed. The recipe takes the environment's id as a param: the plan copies it from the dashboard, `railway status`, or a line that outputs it; the recipe does not look environments up by name (their naming is not documented).
- **RY8** **(unverified)**: Deleting a variable whose environment Railway already removed (the pull request closed) is an error saying the environment was not found, which the adapter reads as already gone; deleting a variable that does not exist answers `true`.
- **RY9** **(unverified)**: Sponson does not wait for the redeploy a write triggers (RY5): a step that needs the running service to see the value waits on Railway's deployment status itself. A reference value written as `${{…}}` is not supported in a plan, where `${…}` is Sponson's own interpolation.

### `railway.variable`

**Variable of a service in an environment** (`http.resource`). One variable of a service (or, without `service_id`, a shared variable) in a Railway environment, typically the PR environment Railway created. Upserted with `variableUpsert`, read unrendered from `variables`, removed with `variableDelete`. A console edit of the value is drift. Railway redeploys the service after each write unless `skip_deploys` is set; Sponson does not wait for that deploy (RY9).

Covers: `railway-variables` in [the coverage matrix](coverage.md#coverage-matrix). Outputs: `id`. On destroy: deleted (`destroy: keep` on the line leaves it).

| Param | Type | Required | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `project_id` | string | yes | — | The project's id. |
| `environment_id` | string | yes | — | The environment's id (for a PR environment, the one Railway created for the pull request; RY7). |
| `service_id` | string | no | — | The service's id; without it, the variable is shared by the environment's services. |
| `name` | string | yes | — | The variable's name. Matches `^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$`. |
| `value` | string | yes | — | The variable's value (may be a `{ secret }` reference). |
| `skip_deploys` | boolean | no | — | Do not redeploy the service after a write (Railway's default is to redeploy). |

```yaml
# under changes: (no provider block needed)
- id: variable
  adapter: http
  op: resource
  recipe: railway.variable
  project_id: prj-railway-demo
  environment_id: env-pr-42
  service_id: svc-web
  name: API_URL
  value: https://api-${ctx.scope}.example.app
```

What the line expands into: the [`http.resource`](plan-format.md#httpresource) params, `{ param: <name> }` standing for a param's value, `{ join: [...] }` for its parts joined into one string, and `{<name>}` in a path for its URI-encoded value.

```yaml
read:
  graphql:
    query: "query variables($projectId: String!, $environmentId: String!, $serviceId: String, $unrendered: Boolean) { variables(projectId: $projectId, environmentId: $environmentId, serviceId: $serviceId, unrendered: $unrendered) }"
    variables:
      projectId: { param: project_id }
      environmentId: { param: environment_id }
      serviceId: { param: service_id }
      unrendered: true
    data_path:
      join:
        - /variables/
        - { param: name }
create:
  graphql:
    query: "mutation variableUpsert($input: VariableUpsertInput!) { variableUpsert(input: $input) }"
    variables:
      input:
        projectId: { param: project_id }
        environmentId: { param: environment_id }
        serviceId: { param: service_id }
        name: { param: name }
        value: { param: value }
        skipDeploys: { param: skip_deploys }
    idempotent: true
update:
  graphql:
    query: "mutation variableUpsert($input: VariableUpsertInput!) { variableUpsert(input: $input) }"
    variables:
      input:
        projectId: { param: project_id }
        environmentId: { param: environment_id }
        serviceId: { param: service_id }
        name: { param: name }
        value: { param: value }
        skipDeploys: { param: skip_deploys }
    idempotent: true
delete:
  graphql:
    query: "mutation variableDelete($input: VariableDeleteInput!) { variableDelete(input: $input) }"
    variables:
      input:
        projectId: { param: project_id }
        environmentId: { param: environment_id }
        serviceId: { param: service_id }
        name: { param: name }
fields:
  value: { param: value }
```

## Render

Recipe file: [`packages/adapters/recipes/render.yaml`](../packages/adapters/recipes/render.yaml). Verified on 2026-10-11 against:

- [Authentication](https://api-docs.render.com/reference/authentication)
- [Retrieve environment variable](https://api-docs.render.com/reference/retrieve-env-var)
- [Add or update environment variable](https://api-docs.render.com/reference/update-env-var)
- [Delete environment variable](https://api-docs.render.com/reference/delete-env-var)
- [Update environment variables (replace all; deploy behaviour)](https://api-docs.render.com/reference/update-env-vars-for-service)
- [Service previews](https://render.com/docs/service-previews)
- [Render CLI (RENDER_API_KEY)](https://render.com/docs/cli)

| API default | Value |
|---|---|
| `base_url` | `https://api.render.com/v1` |
| `base_url_env` | `RENDER_API_URL` |
| Credential | `RENDER_API_KEY` (bearer) |

Assumptions:

- **RE1** (verified, [source](https://api-docs.render.com/reference/authentication)): Requests authenticate with an API key as `Authorization: Bearer`; the Render CLI reads it from `RENDER_API_KEY`.
- **RE2** (verified, [source](https://api-docs.render.com/reference/retrieve-env-var)): `GET /services/{serviceId}/env-vars/{envVarKey}` answers the variable bare, `{ key, value }`, and 404 when it does not exist.
- **RE3** (verified, [source](https://api-docs.render.com/reference/update-env-var)): `PUT /services/{serviceId}/env-vars/{envVarKey}` with `{ value }` adds the variable or replaces its value (200, `{ key, value }`): a create whose answer was lost is the same request again, and the variable's name is its identity.
- **RE4** (verified, [source](https://api-docs.render.com/reference/delete-env-var)): `DELETE /services/{serviceId}/env-vars/{envVarKey}` removes the variable (204).
- **RE5** **(unverified)**: Deleting a variable that is already gone answers 404 (documented only as "Unable to find the requested resource"), which destroy treats as done.
- **RE6** (verified, [source](https://api-docs.render.com/reference/update-env-vars-for-service)): Changing environment variables through the API does not deploy the service, whatever its autoDeploy setting (stated for the replace-all endpoint); a running preview sees a new value only after its next deploy.
- **RE7** **(unverified)**: The single-variable PUT does not deploy either (its page is silent; assumed like the replace-all endpoint).
- **RE8** (verified, [source](https://render.com/docs/service-previews)): Render creates service previews and preview environments itself (per pull request, from the service's Previews setting or `render.yaml`); a preview copies the base service's variables once, when it is created. No API looks up the preview of pull request N, so the line takes the service's id.
- **RE9** **(unverified)**: `GET` returns the value in plain text for every variable, including ones generated with `generateValue`, so the value can be compared for drift.

### `render.env_var`

**Service environment variable** (`http.resource`). One environment variable on a Render service, such as a preview service's `API_URL`, written by name (`PUT` adds or replaces it). A console edit of its value is drift; destroy deletes it. The service's id is a param: Render creates preview services itself, and writing a variable does not deploy (RE6).

Covers: `render-env` in [the coverage matrix](coverage.md#coverage-matrix). Outputs: `id`. On destroy: deleted (`destroy: keep` on the line leaves it).

| Param | Type | Required | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `service_id` | string | yes | — | The service's id (`srv-…`, in the service's dashboard URL and settings). Matches `^[a-z]{3}-[a-z0-9]+$`. |
| `key` | string | yes | — | The variable's name. Matches `^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$`. |
| `value` | string | yes | — | The variable's value: a literal, `{ from }` or `{ secret }`. |

```yaml

- id: env_var
  adapter: http
  op: resource
  recipe: render.env_var
  service_id: srv-d0a1b2c3d4e5f6g7h8i9
  key: API_URL
  value: https://api-${ctx.scope}.example.com
```

## Resend

Recipe file: [`packages/adapters/recipes/resend.yaml`](../packages/adapters/recipes/resend.yaml). Verified on 2026-10-11 against:

- [Create API key](https://resend.com/docs/api-reference/api-keys/create-api-key)
- [List API keys](https://resend.com/docs/api-reference/api-keys/list-api-keys)
- [Delete API key](https://resend.com/docs/api-reference/api-keys/delete-api-key)
- [Create webhook](https://resend.com/docs/api-reference/webhooks/create-webhook)
- [Retrieve webhook](https://resend.com/docs/api-reference/webhooks/get-webhook)
- [List webhooks](https://resend.com/docs/api-reference/webhooks/list-webhooks)
- [Update webhook](https://resend.com/docs/api-reference/webhooks/update-webhook)
- [Delete webhook](https://resend.com/docs/api-reference/webhooks/delete-webhook)

| API default | Value |
|---|---|
| `base_url` | `https://api.resend.com` |
| `base_url_env` | `RESEND_API_URL` |
| Credential | `RESEND_API_KEY` (bearer) |

Assumptions:

- **RS1** (verified, [source](https://resend.com/docs/api-reference/api-keys/create-api-key)): `POST /api-keys` creates an API key from `name` (at most 50 characters), `permission` (`full_access` or `sending_access`) and `domain_id` (with `sending_access` only), answering `{ id, token }`; requests carry `Authorization: Bearer <key>`.
- **RS2** (verified, [source](https://resend.com/docs/api-reference/api-keys/list-api-keys)): `GET /api-keys` answers `{ object: list, has_more, data: [{ id, name, created_at, last_used_at }] }`, every key when no `limit` is sent, and never the token: the token is shown only in the create answer, so it is a once-only output.
- **RS3** (verified, [source](https://resend.com/docs/api-reference/api-keys/delete-api-key)): `DELETE /api-keys/{api_key_id}` removes a key; there is no endpoint to read or change one key, so its permission and domain are sent on create and never compared.
- **RS4** (verified, [source](https://resend.com/docs/api-reference/webhooks/create-webhook)): `POST /webhooks` creates a webhook from `endpoint` and `events` (both required), answering `{ object, id, signing_secret }`.
- **RS5** (verified, [source](https://resend.com/docs/api-reference/webhooks/get-webhook)): `GET /webhooks/{webhook_id}` answers the webhook with `status` (`enabled`/`disabled`), `endpoint`, `events` and `signing_secret`: the secret stays readable, so it is an ordinary sensitive output.
- **RS6** (verified, [source](https://resend.com/docs/api-reference/webhooks/list-webhooks)): `GET /webhooks` answers `{ object: list, has_more, data: [{ id, created_at, status, endpoint, events }] }`, every webhook when no `limit` is sent.
- **RS7** (verified, [source](https://resend.com/docs/api-reference/webhooks/update-webhook)): `PATCH /webhooks/{webhook_id}` changes `endpoint`, `events` and `status`; `DELETE` on the same path removes the webhook.
- **RS8** **(unverified)**: Key names and webhook endpoints are not unique in Resend: the recipe takes the name (keys) and the endpoint URL (webhooks) as the identity, and refuses (PARAM_INVALID) when two match, so give each environment its own name and URL.
- **RS9** **(unverified)**: Creating a key or a webhook needs a `full_access` key; a deleted object answers 404.

### `resend.api_key`

**API key** (`http.resource`). A restricted API key per environment, such as `sponson-preview-pr-42` allowed only to send from one domain. Its token is a once-only output: pass it to the app's environment line in the same run (`{ from: <line>.token }`); later runs keep what that line holds, and `apply --recreate <line>` issues a new one. Only its existence is compared for drift: Resend shows no permission or domain for a key.

Covers: `resend-key-webhook` in [the coverage matrix](coverage.md#coverage-matrix). Outputs: `id`, `token` (sensitive, [once](plan-format.md#once-only-outputs): only from the create). On destroy: deleted (`destroy: keep` on the line leaves it).

| Param | Type | Required | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | — | The key's name, unique among the account's keys (RS8); its identity. Matches `^.{1,50}$`. |
| `permission` | string | no | `sending_access` | What the key may do. One of `full_access`, `sending_access`. |
| `domain_id` | string | no | — | With `sending_access`, the only domain the key may send from. |

```yaml
# under changes: (no provider block needed)
- id: api_key
  adapter: http
  op: resource
  recipe: resend.api_key
  name: sponson-${ctx.env}-${ctx.scope}
```

What the line expands into: the [`http.resource`](plan-format.md#httpresource) params, `{ param: <name> }` standing for a param's value and `{<name>}` in a path for its URI-encoded value.

```yaml
find:
  path: /api-keys
  list_path: /data
  match:
    name: { param: name }
create:
  path: /api-keys
  body:
    permission: { param: permission }
    domain_id: { param: domain_id }
delete:
  path: /api-keys/{id}
outputs:
  token:
    path: /token
    sensitive: true
    once: true
```

### `resend.webhook`

**Webhook** (`http.resource`). A webhook delivering an environment's email events to its URL, such as the preview's `/api/resend` handler. Located by its endpoint URL; a console edit of its events is drift (its enabled/disabled status is left to the console: the create request takes none). Its signing secret is a sensitive output, readable on every run.

Covers: `resend-key-webhook` in [the coverage matrix](coverage.md#coverage-matrix). Outputs: `id`, `signing_secret` (sensitive). On destroy: deleted (`destroy: keep` on the line leaves it).

| Param | Type | Required | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `endpoint` | string | yes | — | The URL events are delivered to; its identity (RS8). Matches `^https://\\S+$`. |
| `events` | list | yes | — | The event types to deliver, such as `email.delivered` and `email.bounced`. |

```yaml
# under changes: (no provider block needed)
- id: webhook
  adapter: http
  op: resource
  recipe: resend.webhook
  endpoint: https://${ctx.scope}.preview.example.com/api/resend
  events:
    - email.delivered
    - email.bounced
```

What the line expands into: the [`http.resource`](plan-format.md#httpresource) params, `{ param: <name> }` standing for a param's value and `{<name>}` in a path for its URI-encoded value.

```yaml
find:
  path: /webhooks
  list_path: /data
  match:
    endpoint: { param: endpoint }
read:
  path: /webhooks/{id}
create:
  path: /webhooks
update:
  method: PATCH
  path: /webhooks/{id}
delete:
  path: /webhooks/{id}
fields:
  events: { param: events }
outputs:
  signing_secret:
    path: /signing_secret
    sensitive: true
```

## Amazon S3 / Cloudflare R2 (S3 API)

Recipe file: [`packages/adapters/recipes/s3.yaml`](../packages/adapters/recipes/s3.yaml). Verified on 2026-10-11 against:

- [PutBucketCors](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/API/API_PutBucketCors.html)
- [GetBucketCors](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/API/API_GetBucketCors.html)
- [DeleteBucketCors](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/API/API_DeleteBucketCors.html)
- [R2 S3 API compatibility](https://developers.cloudflare.com/r2/api/s3/api/)

| API default | Value |
|---|---|
| `base_url` | none: set it in the provider block |
| `base_url_env` | `S3_API_URL` |
| Credential | `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` / `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` (AWS SigV4, `s3` in `us-east-1`) |
| `encoding` | `xml` |

Assumptions:

- **SS1** (verified, [source](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/API/API_PutBucketCors.html)): `PUT /?cors` on the bucket's endpoint replaces its whole CORS configuration with a `CORSConfiguration` document of up to 100 `CORSRule`s (each `ID`, `AllowedOrigin`s, `AllowedMethod`s, `AllowedHeader`s, `ExposeHeader`s, `MaxAgeSeconds`) and requires `Content-MD5`, which the SigV4 signer adds for `s3`.
- **SS2** (verified, [source](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/API/API_GetBucketCors.html)): `GET /?cors` answers the configuration as XML.
- **SS3** (verified, [source](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/API/API_DeleteBucketCors.html)): `DELETE /?cors` removes the configuration (the way to leave a bucket with no rule).
- **SS4** (verified, [source](https://developers.cloudflare.com/r2/api/s3/api/)): R2 implements PutBucketCors, GetBucketCors and DeleteBucketCors at `https://<ACCOUNT_ID>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com`; its SigV4 region is `auto`, and `us-east-1` is accepted as an alias, so the recipe's region works for R2 unchanged.
- **SS5** **(unverified)**: A bucket without a CORS configuration answers 404 `NoSuchCORSConfiguration` (read as an empty list, `parent.if_missing: empty`), and an empty configuration is refused as `MalformedXML` (so the last rule is removed with DELETE, `parent.when_empty: delete`).
- **SS6** **(unverified)**: R2 accepts path-style requests (`https://<ACCOUNT_ID>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com/<bucket>/?cors`), so its base URL names the bucket in the path.
- **SS7** **(unverified)**: S3 answers a rule's elements as they were written; a rule's `ID` identifies it among the bucket's rules (IDs are not required to be unique by S3, so other writers must not reuse the recipe's).

### `s3.bucket_cors`

**CORS rule of a bucket** (`http.list_item`). A CORS rule of an S3 or R2 bucket allowing the preview's origin, identified by its `ID` (such as `sponson-pr-42`); every other rule is left as it is. The base URL names the bucket: `https://<bucket>.s3.<region>.amazonaws.com` (set `auth.aws_sigv4.region` to the bucket's region), or `https://<account>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com/<bucket>` for R2. A console edit of the rule is drift; destroy removes only this rule (the whole configuration when it was the last one).

Covers: `s3-r2-cors` in [the coverage matrix](coverage.md#coverage-matrix). Outputs: none. On destroy: deleted (`destroy: keep` on the line leaves it).

| Param | Type | Required | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `rule_id` | string | yes | — | The rule's `ID`, at most 255 characters; its identity (SS7). Matches `^.{1,255}$`. |
| `origin` | string | yes | — | The origin allowed (the preview's URL, without a path). Matches `^(https?://\\S+\|\\*)$`. |
| `methods` | list | no | `["GET"]` | The methods allowed: `GET`, `PUT`, `POST`, `DELETE`, `HEAD`. |
| `allowed_headers` | list | no | — | Request headers a preflight may ask for (`*` for any); absent: none. |
| `expose_headers` | list | no | — | Response headers the browser may read; absent, none. |
| `max_age_seconds` | string | no | `3000` | How long a preflight answer may be cached, in seconds (a string, as XML carries it). Matches `^[0-9]+$`. |

```yaml
providers:
  http:
    s3:
      recipe: s3
      base_url: https://assets.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com
changes:
  - id: bucket_cors
    adapter: http
    op: list_item
    recipe: s3.bucket_cors
    rule_id: sponson-${ctx.scope}
    origin: https://${ctx.scope}.preview.example.app
```

What the line expands into: the [`http.list_item`](plan-format.md#httplist_item) params, `{ param: <name> }` standing for a param's value and `{<name>}` in a path for its URI-encoded value.

```yaml
parent:
  path: /?cors
  method: PUT
  if_missing: empty
  when_empty: delete
list_path: /CORSConfiguration/CORSRule
key_field: ID
item:
  AllowedHeader: { param: allowed_headers }
  AllowedMethod: { param: methods }
  AllowedOrigin: { param: origin }
  ExposeHeader: { param: expose_headers }
  ID: { param: rule_id }
  MaxAgeSeconds: { param: max_age_seconds }
```

## SendGrid

Recipe file: [`packages/adapters/recipes/sendgrid.yaml`](../packages/adapters/recipes/sendgrid.yaml). Verified on 2026-10-11 against:

- [Create an Event Webhook](https://www.twilio.com/docs/sendgrid/api-reference/webhooks/create-an-event-webhook)
- [Get all Event Webhooks](https://www.twilio.com/docs/sendgrid/api-reference/webhooks/get-all-event-webhooks)
- [Get an Event Webhook](https://www.twilio.com/docs/sendgrid/api-reference/webhooks/get-an-event-webhook)
- [Update an Event Webhook](https://www.twilio.com/docs/sendgrid/api-reference/webhooks/update-an-event-webhook)
- [Delete an Event Webhook](https://www.twilio.com/docs/sendgrid/api-reference/webhooks/delete-an-event-webhook)
- [Create a parse setting](https://www.twilio.com/docs/sendgrid/api-reference/settings-inbound-parse/create-a-parse-setting)
- [Retrieve a specific parse setting](https://www.twilio.com/docs/sendgrid/api-reference/settings-inbound-parse/retrieve-a-specific-parse-setting)
- [Update a parse setting](https://www.twilio.com/docs/sendgrid/api-reference/settings-inbound-parse/update-a-parse-setting)
- [Delete a parse setting](https://www.twilio.com/docs/sendgrid/api-reference/settings-inbound-parse/delete-a-parse-setting)

| API default | Value |
|---|---|
| `base_url` | `https://api.sendgrid.com` |
| `base_url_env` | `SENDGRID_API_URL` |
| Credential | `SENDGRID_API_KEY` (bearer) |

Assumptions:

- **SG1** (verified, [source](https://www.twilio.com/docs/sendgrid/api-reference/webhooks/create-an-event-webhook)): `POST /v3/user/webhooks/event/settings` creates an Event Webhook from `url` (required), `enabled`, one boolean per event type (`processed`, `delivered`, `dropped`, `deferred`, `bounce`, `open`, `click`, `spam_report`, `unsubscribe`, `group_unsubscribe`, `group_resubscribe`) and `friendly_name`, answering 201 with the webhook and its string `id`; requests carry the API key as `Authorization: Bearer`. EU regional subusers use `https://api.eu.sendgrid.com`.
- **SG2** (verified, [source](https://www.twilio.com/docs/sendgrid/api-reference/webhooks/create-an-event-webhook)): Each URL can be used by only one Event Webhook (a second create answers 400 naming the existing id), so the URL identifies the webhook; the number of webhooks is limited by the plan (400 beyond it).
- **SG3** (verified, [source](https://www.twilio.com/docs/sendgrid/api-reference/webhooks/get-all-event-webhooks)): `GET /v3/user/webhooks/event/settings/all` answers `{ max_allowed, webhooks: [...] }` with every webhook's settings and `id`.
- **SG4** (verified, [source](https://www.twilio.com/docs/sendgrid/api-reference/webhooks/update-an-event-webhook)): `PATCH /v3/user/webhooks/event/settings/{id}` requires `url` and updates the fields sent; `DELETE` on the same path answers 204, and 404 for an unknown id. Without an id these paths act on the oldest webhook, which the recipe never does (its paths always carry the id).
- **SG5** (verified, [source](https://www.twilio.com/docs/sendgrid/api-reference/webhooks/create-an-event-webhook)): Signature verification and its public key are set through a separate endpoint and are not part of the webhook's create or update; this recipe does not manage them.
- **SG6** (verified, [source](https://www.twilio.com/docs/sendgrid/api-reference/settings-inbound-parse/create-a-parse-setting)): `POST /v3/user/webhooks/parse/settings` creates an Inbound Parse setting from `url`, `hostname`, `spam_check` and `send_raw`, answering 201 with those four fields bare; `GET`, `PATCH` and `DELETE` (204) `/v3/user/webhooks/parse/settings/{hostname}` read, update and remove it. The hostname must be on a domain authenticated in SendGrid, with an MX record pointing at SendGrid.
- **SG7** **(unverified)**: A PATCH that leaves out an event flag keeps its current value (the documentation's examples send only `url`); the recipe sends every flag it compares anyway.
- **SG8** **(unverified)**: A parse setting for a hostname that exists already is refused with an error status (not documented which); the next run then finds it by its hostname.

### `sendgrid.event_webhook`

**Event Webhook** (`http.resource`). An Event Webhook delivering an environment's email events to its URL, such as the preview's `/api/sendgrid/events` handler. Located by its URL (unique in SendGrid); a console edit of its enabled flag, an event flag or its friendly name is drift.

Covers: `sendgrid-webhook` in [the coverage matrix](coverage.md#coverage-matrix). Outputs: `id`. On destroy: deleted (`destroy: keep` on the line leaves it).

| Param | Type | Required | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `url` | string | yes | — | The URL events are posted to; its identity (SG2). Matches `^https?://\\S+$`. |
| `enabled` | boolean | no | `true` | Whether events are posted. |
| `friendly_name` | string | no | — | A label for the webhook (not unique). |
| `processed` | boolean | no | `false` | Post `processed` events. |
| `delivered` | boolean | no | `true` | Post `delivered` events. |
| `dropped` | boolean | no | `true` | Post `dropped` events. |
| `deferred` | boolean | no | `false` | Post `deferred` events. |
| `bounce` | boolean | no | `true` | Post `bounce` events. |
| `open` | boolean | no | `false` | Post `open` events. |
| `click` | boolean | no | `false` | Post `click` events. |
| `spam_report` | boolean | no | `true` | Post `spam_report` events. |
| `unsubscribe` | boolean | no | `false` | Post `unsubscribe` events. |
| `group_unsubscribe` | boolean | no | `false` | Post `group_unsubscribe` events. |
| `group_resubscribe` | boolean | no | `false` | Post `group_resubscribe` events. |

```yaml
# under changes: (no provider block needed)
- id: event_webhook
  adapter: http
  op: resource
  recipe: sendgrid.event_webhook
  url: https://${ctx.scope}.preview.example.com/api/sendgrid/events
  friendly_name: sponson ${ctx.env} ${ctx.scope}
```

What the line expands into: the [`http.resource`](plan-format.md#httpresource) params, `{ param: <name> }` standing for a param's value and `{<name>}` in a path for its URI-encoded value.

```yaml
find:
  path: /v3/user/webhooks/event/settings/all
  list_path: /webhooks
  match:
    url: { param: url }
create:
  path: /v3/user/webhooks/event/settings
update:
  method: PATCH
  path: /v3/user/webhooks/event/settings/{id}
  body:
    url: { param: url }
delete:
  path: /v3/user/webhooks/event/settings/{id}
fields:
  enabled: { param: enabled }
  friendly_name: { param: friendly_name }
  processed: { param: processed }
  delivered: { param: delivered }
  dropped: { param: dropped }
  deferred: { param: deferred }
  bounce: { param: bounce }
  open: { param: open }
  click: { param: click }
  spam_report: { param: spam_report }
  unsubscribe: { param: unsubscribe }
  group_unsubscribe: { param: group_unsubscribe }
  group_resubscribe: { param: group_resubscribe }
```

### `sendgrid.parse_setting`

**Inbound Parse setting** (`http.resource`). An Inbound Parse host per environment, such as `pr-42.parse.example.com`, posting the mail it receives to the environment's URL. Named by its hostname; a console edit of its URL, spam check or raw flag is drift. The hostname's domain must be authenticated in SendGrid and its MX record point at SendGrid (a wildcard record serves every environment).

Covers: `sendgrid-webhook` in [the coverage matrix](coverage.md#coverage-matrix). Outputs: `id`. On destroy: deleted (`destroy: keep` on the line leaves it).

| Param | Type | Required | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `hostname` | string | yes | — | The host mail is received for, lower-case; its identity. Matches `^[a-z0-9.-]+$`. |
| `url` | string | yes | — | The URL parsed mail is posted to. Matches `^https?://\\S+$`. |
| `spam_check` | boolean | no | `false` | Check mail for spam before posting it. |
| `send_raw` | boolean | no | `false` | Post the original MIME message. |

```yaml
# under changes: (no provider block needed)
- id: parse_setting
  adapter: http
  op: resource
  recipe: sendgrid.parse_setting
  hostname: ${ctx.scope}.parse.example.com
  url: https://${ctx.scope}.preview.example.com/api/sendgrid/inbound
```

What the line expands into: the [`http.resource`](plan-format.md#httpresource) params, `{ param: <name> }` standing for a param's value and `{<name>}` in a path for its URI-encoded value.

```yaml
read:
  path: /v3/user/webhooks/parse/settings/{hostname}
create:
  path: /v3/user/webhooks/parse/settings
  body:
    hostname: { param: hostname }
update:
  method: PATCH
id_path: /hostname
fields:
  url: { param: url }
  spam_check: { param: spam_check }
  send_raw: { param: send_raw }
```

## Sentry

Recipe file: [`packages/adapters/recipes/sentry.yaml`](../packages/adapters/recipes/sentry.yaml). Verified on 2026-10-11 against:

- [Create a New Release for an Organization](https://docs.sentry.io/api/releases/create-a-new-release-for-an-organization/)
- [Retrieve an Organization's Release](https://docs.sentry.io/api/releases/retrieve-an-organizations-release/)
- [Update an Organization's Release](https://docs.sentry.io/api/releases/update-an-organizations-release/)
- [Delete an Organization's Release](https://docs.sentry.io/api/releases/delete-an-organizations-release/)
- [Create a Deploy](https://docs.sentry.io/api/releases/create-a-deploy/)
- [List a Release's Deploys](https://docs.sentry.io/api/releases/list-a-releases-deploys/)
- [Release Management (sentry-cli)](https://docs.sentry.io/cli/releases/)

| API default | Value |
|---|---|
| `base_url` | `https://sentry.io/api/0` |
| `base_url_env` | `SENTRY_API_URL` |
| Credential | `SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN` (bearer) |

Assumptions:

- **SE1** (verified, [source](https://docs.sentry.io/api/releases/create-a-new-release-for-an-organization/)): `POST /api/0/organizations/{organization_id_or_slug}/releases/` creates a release from `version` and `projects` (both required), `ref`, `url`, `dateReleased` and commit data, with a bearer token holding `project:releases`, `project:write`, `project:admin` or `org:ci`; it answers 201 (or 208).
- **SE2** (verified, [source](https://docs.sentry.io/api/releases/retrieve-an-organizations-release/)): A version is one release across the organization's projects, and `GET /api/0/organizations/{org}/releases/{version}/` answers it (404 when there is none), so the version names the release.
- **SE3** (verified, [source](https://docs.sentry.io/api/releases/update-an-organizations-release/)): `PUT /api/0/organizations/{org}/releases/{version}/` updates `ref`, `url`, `dateReleased` and commit data (the documentation says an omitted `dateReleased` is the current time), and answers the release.
- **SE4** (verified, [source](https://docs.sentry.io/api/releases/delete-an-organizations-release/)): `DELETE /api/0/organizations/{org}/releases/{version}/` permanently removes a release and its files (`project:releases` or `project:admin`). The recipe keeps releases on destroy: one version is shared by every environment it is deployed to.
- **SE5** (verified, [source](https://docs.sentry.io/api/releases/create-a-deploy/)): `POST /api/0/organizations/{org}/releases/{version}/deploys/` records a deploy of the release from `environment` (required), `name`, `url`, `dateStarted`, `dateFinished` (default now) and `projects` (default: all of the release's).
- **SE6** (verified, [source](https://docs.sentry.io/cli/releases/)): `GET /api/0/organizations/{org}/releases/{version}/deploys/` lists the release's deploys; deploys cannot be deleted, so the deploy op never deletes (`destroy: never`).
- **SE7** (verified, [source](https://docs.sentry.io/api/releases/create-a-new-release-for-an-organization/)): The release's `dateReleased` defaults to the current time on create, so a release this recipe creates is finalized at once.
- **SE8** **(unverified)**: A create for a version that exists answers 208 with the existing release (not an error), so a release another tool made (sentry-cli in the build) is taken over without a second write; the recipe keeps it on destroy either way.
- **SE9** **(unverified)**: The deploy list answers a bare array of `{ id, environment, name, url, dateStarted, dateFinished }` with string ids, all of a release's deploys on the first page; `environment` and `name` together identify the deploy this recipe recorded.
- **SE10** **(unverified)**: Release `url` is answered as sent (null when unset); organizations hosted in another region (`de.sentry.io`) or self-hosted Sentry set `base_url` in the provider block.

### `sentry.release`

**Release** (`http.resource`). A release for the commit, such as `app@${ctx.git.sha}`, in the given projects, finalized when created (SE7). Named by its version; a console edit of its URL is drift. Kept on destroy (shared history: preview and production deploy the same version); `destroy: delete` on the line removes it.

Covers: `sentry-release` in [the coverage matrix](coverage.md#coverage-matrix). Outputs: `id`. On destroy: left in place by default (`destroy: delete` on the line removes it).

| Param | Type | Required | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `organization` | string | yes | — | The organization's slug or id. |
| `version` | string | yes | — | The release's version (no slashes or whitespace), such as `app@<sha>`. Matches `^[^/\\s]+$`. |
| `project` | string | yes | — | The slug of the project the release belongs to (a release of several projects is a hand-written `http` line). |
| `url` | string | no | — | A link for the release (its commit or build). |
| `ref` | string | no | — | A commit reference, sent on create. |

```yaml
# under changes: (no provider block needed)
- id: release
  adapter: http
  op: resource
  recipe: sentry.release
  organization: acme
  version: app@${ctx.git.sha}
  project: web
  url: https://github.com/acme/app/commit/${ctx.git.sha}
```

What the line expands into: the [`http.resource`](plan-format.md#httpresource) params, `{ param: <name> }` standing for a param's value and `{<name>}` in a path for its URI-encoded value.

```yaml
read:
  path: /organizations/{organization}/releases/{version}/
create:
  path: /organizations/{organization}/releases/
  body:
    version: { param: version }
    projects:
      - { param: project }
    ref: { param: ref }
update:
  method: PUT
id_path: /version
fields:
  url: { param: url }
```

### `sentry.deploy`

**Deploy of a release to an environment** (`http.resource`). The record that a release was deployed to an environment (`preview`, named for the scope), which Sentry shows on the release and uses for deploy notifications. Located by environment and name among the release's deploys. Sentry has no way to change or delete a deploy, so nothing is compared for drift and destroy leaves it (`destroy: never`).

Covers: `sentry-release` in [the coverage matrix](coverage.md#coverage-matrix). Outputs: `id`. On destroy: left in place: the provider offers no way to delete it (`destroy: delete` is refused).

| Param | Type | Required | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `organization` | string | yes | — | The organization's slug or id. |
| `version` | string | yes | — | The deployed release's version; the release must exist (`{ from: <release line>.id }` orders the lines). Matches `^[^/\\s]+$`. |
| `environment` | string | yes | — | The environment deployed to. |
| `name` | string | yes | — | The deploy's name, which with the environment identifies it among the release's deploys. |
| `url` | string | no | — | A link to the deployment (the preview URL), sent on create. |

```yaml
# under changes: (no provider block needed)
- id: deploy
  adapter: http
  op: resource
  recipe: sentry.deploy
  organization: acme
  version: app@${ctx.git.sha}
  environment: ${ctx.env}
  name: sponson-${ctx.scope}
```

What the line expands into: the [`http.resource`](plan-format.md#httpresource) params, `{ param: <name> }` standing for a param's value and `{<name>}` in a path for its URI-encoded value.

```yaml
find:
  path: /organizations/{organization}/releases/{version}/deploys/
  match:
    environment: { param: environment }
    name: { param: name }
create:
  path: /organizations/{organization}/releases/{version}/deploys/
  body:
    url: { param: url }
delete:
  path: /organizations/{organization}/releases/{version}/deploys/{id}/
```

## Split (Harness FME)

Recipe file: [`packages/adapters/recipes/split.yaml`](../packages/adapters/recipes/split.yaml). Verified on 2026-10-11 against:

- [Authentication](https://docs.split.io/reference/authentication)
- [Get feature flag definition in environment](https://docs.split.io/reference/get-feature-flag-definition-in-environment)
- [Full update feature flag definition in environment](https://docs.split.io/reference/full-update-feature-flag-definition-in-environment)
- [Feature flag definition, rule, condition, matcher](https://docs.split.io/reference/feature-flag-definition)
- [Matcher types](https://docs.split.io/reference/matcher-type)
- [API for Split admins after the move to Harness](https://developer.harness.io/docs/feature-management-experimentation/split-to-harness/api-for-split-admins/)

| API default | Value |
|---|---|
| `base_url` | `https://api.split.io/internal/api/v2` |
| `base_url_env` | `SPLIT_API_URL` |
| Credential | `SPLIT_ADMIN_API_KEY` (bearer) |

Assumptions:

- **SP1** (verified, [source](https://developer.harness.io/docs/feature-management-experimentation/split-to-harness/api-for-split-admins/)): The Admin API is at `https://api.split.io/internal/api/v2`, authenticated as `Authorization: Bearer` with a Split Admin API key (or a Harness PAT/SAT, accepted as Bearer on the non-deprecated endpoints). Host and paths are unchanged by the move to Harness; the workspace id is still Split's `wsId`.
- **SP2** (verified, [source](https://docs.split.io/reference/get-feature-flag-definition-in-environment)): `GET /splits/ws/{wsId}/{featureFlagName}/environments/{environmentIdOrName}` answers the flag's definition in the environment bare: `treatments`, `defaultTreatment`, `baselineTreatment`, `trafficAllocation`, `rules`, `defaultRule` and read-only fields (`name`, `environment`, `trafficType`, times).
- **SP3** (verified, [source](https://docs.split.io/reference/full-update-feature-flag-definition-in-environment)): `PUT` on the same path replaces the definition with `treatments`, `defaultTreatment`, `baselineTreatment`, `trafficAllocation`, `rules` and `defaultRule` (the first three of the required fields). Those are sent as read, with the rule list changed (`parent.send`); whether PUT takes the read-only fields back is not documented, so they are not sent.
- **SP4** (verified, [source](https://docs.split.io/reference/matcher-type)): A rule is `{ condition: { combiner: AND, matchers: [...] }, buckets: [{ treatment, size }] }` (bucket sizes sum to 100); rules have no id and are evaluated in order. `IN_LIST_STRING` with `attribute` and `strings` matches an attribute in a list.
- **SP5** **(unverified)**: A rule is read back with its matcher exactly as written (no added `negate: false` or null members); otherwise every plan shows the rule as changed.
- **SP6** **(unverified)**: A full update leaves the flag's killed state alone (`killed` is not a documented PUT field).
- **SP7** (verified, [source](https://developer.harness.io/docs/feature-management-experimentation/api/feature-flags/)): In a project that requires a title and comment on changes, they are query parameters of the update; this recipe does not send them, so such a project refuses the write and the apply fails.

### `split.targeting_rule`

**Feature flag targeting rule** (`http.list_item`). A targeting rule on a feature flag's definition in one environment that serves a treatment to the preview, such as `if preview is in list [pr-42] serve on`. Added after the flag's other rules (evaluated in order: an earlier matching rule wins); the treatments, default rule and traffic allocation are written back as read. Identified by the matched value; a console edit of its matcher or treatment is drift. Destroy removes the rule.

Covers: `split-rule` in [the coverage matrix](coverage.md#coverage-matrix). Outputs: none. On destroy: deleted (`destroy: keep` on the line leaves it).

| Param | Type | Required | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `workspace_id` | string | yes | — | The workspace (project) id, Split's `wsId`. |
| `flag` | string | yes | — | The feature flag's name. |
| `environment` | string | yes | — | The environment's id or name; the flag must have a definition there. |
| `attribute` | string | yes | — | The attribute the rule tests (passed with the evaluation). |
| `match` | string | yes | — | The attribute value that is the preview; it identifies the rule. |
| `treatment` | string | yes | — | The treatment served to the preview; one of the flag's treatments. |

```yaml
# under changes: (no provider block needed)
- id: targeting_rule
  adapter: http
  op: list_item
  recipe: split.targeting_rule
  workspace_id: a3b6f5d0-0e8f-11ee-9b0f-0242ac120002
  flag: new_checkout
  environment: Staging
  attribute: preview
  match: ${ctx.scope}
  treatment: on
```

What the line expands into: the [`http.list_item`](plan-format.md#httplist_item) params, `{ param: <name> }` standing for a param's value and `{<name>}` in a path for its URI-encoded value.

```yaml
parent:
  path: /splits/ws/{workspace_id}/{flag}/environments/{environment}
  method: PUT
  send:
    - treatments
    - defaultTreatment
    - baselineTreatment
    - trafficAllocation
    - defaultRule
list_path: /rules
key_field: /condition/matchers/0/strings/0
item:
  condition:
    combiner: AND
    matchers:
      - type: IN_LIST_STRING
        attribute: { param: attribute }
        strings:
          - { param: match }
  buckets:
    - treatment: { param: treatment }
      size: 100
```

## Statsig

Recipe file: [`packages/adapters/recipes/statsig.yaml`](../packages/adapters/recipes/statsig.yaml). Verified on 2026-10-11 against:

- [Console API introduction (base URL, STATSIG-API-KEY, STATSIG-API-VERSION)](https://docs.statsig.com/console-api/introduction)
- [Add gate rule](https://docs.statsig.com/api-reference/gates/add-gate-rule)
- [Read gate rules](https://docs.statsig.com/api-reference/gates/read-gate-rules)
- [Update gate rules (one rule)](https://docs.statsig.com/api-reference/gates/update-gate-rules)
- [Delete gate rule](https://docs.statsig.com/api-reference/gates/delete-gate-rule)
- [Console API OpenAPI spec (20240601)](https://api.statsig.com/openapi/20240601.json)

| API default | Value |
|---|---|
| `base_url` | `https://statsigapi.net/console/v1` |
| `base_url_env` | `STATSIG_API_URL` |
| Credential | `STATSIG_CONSOLE_API_KEY` (header `STATSIG-API-KEY`) |
| `headers` | {"STATSIG-API-VERSION":"20240601"} |

Assumptions:

- **SG1** (verified, [source](https://docs.statsig.com/console-api/introduction)): The Console API is at `https://statsigapi.net/console/v1`, authenticated with a Console API key in the `STATSIG-API-KEY` header; `STATSIG-API-VERSION: 20240601` (the only version) is optional today and announced as required later, so it is always sent.
- **SG2** (verified, [source](https://docs.statsig.com/api-reference/gates/add-gate-rule)): `POST /gates/{id}/rule` (singular) adds one rule (`name`, `passPercentage`, `conditions`, `environments`) and answers `{ message, data: <the whole gate> }`, not the rule: the new rule is located by name afterwards (`create.locate`).
- **SG3** **(unverified)**: `GET /gates/{id}/rules` answers the rules under `data.rules` (the documented example); the spec's schema says `data` is a list of `{ rules }` objects instead. If the API follows the schema, every read fails with PROVIDER_RESPONSE naming `find.list_path` (it does not create duplicates). The rules of one gate fit on the first page.
- **SG4** (verified, [source](https://docs.statsig.com/api-reference/gates/update-gate-rules)): `PATCH /gates/{id}/rules/{ruleID}` updates the given fields of one rule; `DELETE` on the same path removes it. Rules carry a server-assigned `id`.
- **SG5** **(unverified)**: Rule names are unique within a gate (not documented): the rule is identified by its name, and two rules with that name are PARAM_INVALID rather than a guess.
- **SG6** **(unverified)**: A rule is read back with `conditions` exactly as written (`type`, `operator`, `targetValue`, and `field` when sent). If Statsig adds keys such as `field: null` to a condition, every plan shows the rule as changed.
- **SG7** **(unverified)**: DELETE of a rule that is already gone answers 404 (the spec lists only 200); any other answer fails the destroy rather than passing silently.
- **SG8** **(unverified)**: On a gate that requires reviews, what a Console API rule write does (apply, fail, or open a pending review) is not documented; a write that does not take effect is seen on the next read as missing or changed, never as done.

### `statsig.gate_rule`

**Feature gate rule** (`http.resource`). A rule on an existing feature gate that passes the preview, such as `custom_field preview any [pr-42]`. Located by its name in the gate's rules; a console edit of its pass percentage, conditions or environments is drift. Destroy deletes the rule.

Covers: `statsig-gate-rule` in [the coverage matrix](coverage.md#coverage-matrix). Outputs: `id`. On destroy: deleted (`destroy: keep` on the line leaves it).

| Param | Type | Required | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `gate_id` | string | yes | — | The gate's id (its name in the console URL). |
| `name` | string | yes | — | The rule's name, unique within the gate; it identifies the rule. |
| `condition_type` | string | no | `custom_field` | The condition's type: `custom_field` (with `field`), `url`, `environment_tier`, `user_id` or `email`. One of `custom_field`, `url`, `environment_tier`, `user_id`, `email`. |
| `field` | string | no | — | The custom field's name, for `condition_type` `custom_field`. |
| `operator` | string | no | `any` | The condition's operator: `any`, `none`, `str_contains_any`, … (see the Statsig rule docs). |
| `values` | list | yes | — | The values the condition matches (its `targetValue`). |
| `pass_percentage` | number | no | `100` | The share of matching users that pass (0–100). |
| `environment_names` | list | no | — | The environments the rule applies in (for example `[development, staging]`); all when left out. |

```yaml
# under changes: (no provider block needed)
- id: gate_rule
  adapter: http
  op: resource
  recipe: statsig.gate_rule
  gate_id: new_checkout
  name: preview ${ctx.scope}
  field: preview
  values:
    - ${ctx.scope}
```

What the line expands into: the [`http.resource`](plan-format.md#httpresource) params, `{ param: <name> }` standing for a param's value and `{<name>}` in a path for its URI-encoded value.

```yaml
find:
  path: /gates/{gate_id}/rules
  list_path: /data/rules
  match:
    name: { param: name }
create:
  path: /gates/{gate_id}/rule
  locate: true
update:
  method: PATCH
  path: /gates/{gate_id}/rules/{id}
delete:
  path: /gates/{gate_id}/rules/{id}
fields:
  passPercentage: { param: pass_percentage }
  conditions:
    - type: { param: condition_type }
      field: { param: field }
      operator: { param: operator }
      targetValue: { param: values }
  environments: { param: environment_names }
```

## Stripe

Recipe file: [`packages/adapters/recipes/stripe.yaml`](../packages/adapters/recipes/stripe.yaml). Verified on 2026-10-11 against:

- [Authentication](https://docs.stripe.com/api/authentication)
- [API keys](https://docs.stripe.com/keys)
- [Idempotent requests](https://docs.stripe.com/api/idempotent_requests)
- [Create a webhook endpoint](https://docs.stripe.com/api/webhook_endpoints/create)
- [List all webhook endpoints](https://docs.stripe.com/api/webhook_endpoints/list)
- [Update a webhook endpoint](https://docs.stripe.com/api/webhook_endpoints/update)
- [Delete a webhook endpoint](https://docs.stripe.com/api/webhook_endpoints/delete)
- [Webhooks in the Dashboard (endpoint limit)](https://docs.stripe.com/development/dashboard/webhooks)
- [Create a product](https://docs.stripe.com/api/products/create)
- [Retrieve a product](https://docs.stripe.com/api/products/retrieve)
- [Delete a product](https://docs.stripe.com/api/products/delete)
- [Create a price](https://docs.stripe.com/api/prices/create)
- [List all prices](https://docs.stripe.com/api/prices/list)
- [Update a price](https://docs.stripe.com/api/prices/update)
- [Create a coupon](https://docs.stripe.com/api/coupons/create)

| API default | Value |
|---|---|
| `base_url` | `https://api.stripe.com/v1` |
| `base_url_env` | `STRIPE_API_URL` |
| Credential | `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` (bearer) |
| `encoding` | `form` |
| `refuse_credential` | credentials starting `sk_live_` or `rk_live_` are refused (`PROVIDER_AUTH`) unless `SPONSON_STRIPE_ALLOW_LIVE=1`; a plan cannot override this |

Assumptions:

- **ST1** (verified, [source](https://docs.stripe.com/api/authentication)): The API takes a secret or restricted key as `Authorization: Bearer` (besides Basic), and request bodies form-encoded with bracketed nesting (`metadata[k]=v`, `enabled_events[0]=x`).
- **ST2** (verified, [source](https://docs.stripe.com/keys)): Test-mode keys start with `sk_test_` / `rk_test_`, live-mode keys with `sk_live_` / `rk_live_`; objects of one mode are invisible to the other. The recipe refuses the live prefixes (`refuse_credential`) unless `SPONSON_STRIPE_ALLOW_LIVE=1`.
- **ST3** **(unverified)**: Organization keys (`sk_org_…`) and platform-managed keys do not carry the mode in their prefix, so they are not refused: use a test-mode secret or restricted key for previews.
- **ST4** (verified, [source](https://docs.stripe.com/api/idempotent_requests)): Every v1 `POST` accepts an `Idempotency-Key` (up to 255 characters, kept at least 24 hours); a retry with the same key returns the saved answer, and different parameters under one key are an error.
- **ST5** (verified, [source](https://docs.stripe.com/api/webhook_endpoints/create)): `POST /v1/webhook_endpoints` takes `url`, `enabled_events` (`['*']` for all), `description`, `metadata` and `api_version`, and answers the endpoint with its signing `secret` populated.
- **ST6** (verified, [source](https://docs.stripe.com/api/webhook_endpoints/list)): `GET /v1/webhook_endpoints` (`limit` 1–100) answers `{ data: [...], has_more }` whose endpoints carry `url`, `enabled_events`, `description` and `metadata` but no `secret`: the secret exists only in the create's answer, hence the `once` output.
- **ST7** (verified, [source](https://docs.stripe.com/development/dashboard/webhooks)): An account has at most 16 webhook endpoints, so one list page of 100 holds them all, and at most 16 previews (minus the account's own endpoints) can have one at a time.
- **ST8** (verified, [source](https://docs.stripe.com/api/webhook_endpoints/update)): `POST /v1/webhook_endpoints/{id}` updates `url`, `enabled_events`, `description`, `metadata` and `disabled` in place (the secret is not rotated); `DELETE` on the same path removes the endpoint.
- **ST9** **(unverified)**: The API returns `url`, `enabled_events` and `description` as they were written, `enabled_events` in the order sent, so an unchanged endpoint hashes the same on every plan.
- **ST10** (verified, [source](https://docs.stripe.com/api/products/create)): `POST /v1/products` takes a client-chosen `id` (unique among the account's products), `name`, `description` and `active`; `GET /v1/products/{id}` retrieves it; `POST /v1/products/{id}` updates it.
- **ST11** (verified, [source](https://docs.stripe.com/api/products/delete)): A product can be deleted only while it has no prices, and prices are never deleted, so the recipe archives a product (`active: false`) instead of deleting it.
- **ST12** **(unverified)**: An archived product is still returned by `GET /v1/products/{id}`, and its id stays taken: re-applying a destroyed scope finds it and reactivates it as an adopted object, which a later destroy leaves active.
- **ST13** (verified, [source](https://docs.stripe.com/api/prices/create)): `POST /v1/prices` takes `product`, `currency`, `unit_amount`, `recurring[interval]`, `nickname`, `lookup_key` and `transfer_lookup_key` (which moves the lookup key from the price holding it to the new one).
- **ST14** (verified, [source](https://docs.stripe.com/api/prices/list)): `GET /v1/prices` lists active prices by default, filters by up to 10 `lookup_keys` and by `active`, and answers `{ data: [...] }`.
- **ST15** (verified, [source](https://docs.stripe.com/api/prices/update)): A price's amount, currency and interval cannot change after creation; `POST /v1/prices/{id}` updates `active`, `nickname`, `lookup_key` and `metadata`. There is no delete: the recipe archives (`active: false`).
- **ST16** (verified, [source](https://docs.stripe.com/api/coupons/create)): `POST /v1/coupons` takes a client-chosen `id`, `name`, `percent_off` or `amount_off` with `currency`, `duration` (`once`, `repeating`, `forever`) and `duration_in_months`.
- **ST17** **(unverified)**: `GET /v1/coupons/{id}` retrieves a coupon, `POST /v1/coupons/{id}` updates its `name` and `metadata` only (the discount is fixed), and `DELETE /v1/coupons/{id}` deletes it, after which its id may be used again.
- **ST18** **(unverified)**: Stripe must reach the endpoint's URL over public HTTPS: a preview behind deployment protection (Vercel Authentication) receives no events unless it lets Stripe's requests through.

### `stripe.webhook_endpoint`

**Webhook endpoint** (`http.resource`). A test-mode webhook endpoint that sends the preview's events to its own URL, `url` + `path` (usually `{ from: web.preview_url }`). Identified by `name` in its metadata, so a new preview URL updates the endpoint in place. Its signing `secret` exists only in the answer that creates the endpoint: it is a once-only output, passed in the same run to the line that writes it (`STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` in a `vercel.env` or `netlify.env` line); later runs keep what that line holds, and `apply --recreate <line>` rotates it. Writing the secret rebuilds the preview, and a preview URL output follows the newest deploy, so the next run moves the endpoint to the rebuilt deploy's URL (in place: the secret is kept); a URL that does not change per deploy (`https://deploy-preview-${ctx.pr.number}--<site>.netlify.app`, a custom preview domain) avoids that update. A console edit of its URL, events or description is drift.

Covers: `stripe-webhook` in [the coverage matrix](coverage.md#coverage-matrix). Outputs: `id`, `secret` (sensitive, [once](plan-format.md#once-only-outputs): only from the create). On destroy: deleted (`destroy: keep` on the line leaves it).

| Param | Type | Required | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | — | The endpoint's identity, kept in its metadata (`sponson_endpoint`): unique per preview, such as `preview-${ctx.scope}`. Matches `^[A-Za-z0-9_.:/-]{1,200}$`. |
| `url` | string | yes | — | The preview's base URL, without a trailing slash: usually `{ from: <vercel.env or netlify.env line>.preview_url }`. Matches `^https://\\S*[^/]$`. |
| `path` | string | no | `/api/webhooks/stripe` | The path of the app's webhook handler, appended to `url`. Matches `^/\\S*$`. |
| `enabled_events` | list | no | `["*"]` | The event types sent to the endpoint (`['*']`: all that need no explicit selection). |
| `description` | string | no | — | A note shown in the Dashboard. |
| `api_version` | string | no | — | The Stripe API version events are rendered with (the account's default when left out); sent on create only. |

```yaml
# under changes: (no provider block needed)
- id: webhook_endpoint
  adapter: http
  op: resource
  recipe: stripe.webhook_endpoint
  name: preview-${ctx.scope}
  url: https://pr-42.preview.example.com
  enabled_events:
    - checkout.session.completed
    - customer.subscription.updated
  description: Preview webhook managed by Sponson
```

What the line expands into: the [`http.resource`](plan-format.md#httpresource) params, `{ param: <name> }` standing for a param's value, `{ join: [...] }` for its parts joined into one string, and `{<name>}` in a path for its URI-encoded value.

```yaml
find:
  path: /webhook_endpoints?limit=100
  list_path: /data
  match:
    /metadata/sponson_endpoint: { param: name }
create:
  path: /webhook_endpoints
  idempotency_key: true
  body:
    api_version: { param: api_version }
update:
  method: POST
  path: /webhook_endpoints/{id}
delete:
  path: /webhook_endpoints/{id}
fields:
  url:
    join:
      - { param: url }
      - { param: path }
  enabled_events: { param: enabled_events }
  description: { param: description }
outputs:
  secret:
    path: /secret
    sensitive: true
    once: true
```

Covers: `stripe-test-objects` in [the coverage matrix](coverage.md#coverage-matrix). Outputs: `id`. On destroy: deleted (`destroy: keep` on the line leaves it).

| Param | Type | Required | Default | Meaning |

| `product_id` | string | yes | — | The product's id, unique in the account, such as `pro-${ctx.scope}`. Matches `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,100}$`. |
| `name` | string | yes | — | The product's name, shown to customers. |
| `description` | string | no | — | The product's description, shown to customers. |

```yaml
  adapter: http
```


### `stripe.price`

**Price** (`http.resource`). A test-mode price found by its lookup key (`lookup`, such as `pro-monthly-pr-42`, which the preview's code looks the price up by), product, currency, amount and interval. Amount, currency and interval cannot change on a Stripe price, so changing them in the plan makes a new price that takes over the lookup key, and the old one stays until the scope is destroyed. Destroy archives it (`active: false`): Stripe never deletes a price. A console edit of its nickname is drift.

Covers: `stripe-test-objects` in [the coverage matrix](coverage.md#coverage-matrix). Outputs: `id`. On destroy: deleted (`destroy: keep` on the line leaves it).

| Param | Type | Required | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `lookup` | string | yes | — | The price's `lookup_key`: what the preview's code looks it up by, unique among active prices. (Named `lookup` because a plan key ending in `_key` must hold a secret reference.) Matches `^\\S{1,200}$`. |
| `product` | string | yes | — | The product's id: usually `{ from: <stripe.product line>.id }`. |
| `currency` | string | yes | — | Three-letter ISO currency code, lower-case. Matches `^[a-z]{3}$`. |
| `unit_amount` | integer | yes | — | The amount in the currency's smallest unit (1500 is 15.00 USD). |
| `interval` | string | no | — | The billing interval of a recurring price; left out, the price is one-time. One of `day`, `week`, `month`, `year`. |
| `nickname` | string | no | — | A note on the price, hidden from customers. |

```yaml
# under changes: (no provider block needed)
- id: price
  adapter: http
  op: resource
  recipe: stripe.price
  lookup: pro-monthly-${ctx.scope}
  product: pro-pr-42
  currency: usd
  unit_amount: 1500
  interval: month
  nickname: Pro monthly (preview)
```

What the line expands into: the [`http.resource`](plan-format.md#httpresource) params, `{ param: <name> }` standing for a param's value and `{<name>}` in a path for its URI-encoded value.

```yaml
find:
  path: /prices?lookup_keys[]={lookup}&active=true&limit=10
  list_path: /data
  match:
    lookup_key: { param: lookup }
    active: true
    product: { param: product }
    currency: { param: currency }
    unit_amount: { param: unit_amount }
    /recurring/interval: { param: interval }
create:
  path: /prices
  idempotency_key: true
  body:
    transfer_lookup_key: true
update:
  method: POST
  path: /prices/{id}
delete:
  method: POST
  path: /prices/{id}
  body:
    active: false
fields:
  nickname: { param: nickname }
```

**Coupon** (`http.resource`). A test-mode coupon with an id of the plan's choosing, such as `preview-pr-42`, for the discount codes a preview accepts. Its discount (percent or amount, duration) is set on create and fixed after; give the line a new `coupon_id` to change it. Destroy deletes it. A console edit of its name is drift.

| `amount_off` | integer | no | — | The discount in the currency's smallest unit, with `currency`. |
| `currency` | string | no | — | The currency of `amount_off`. Matches `^[a-z]{3}$`. |
| `duration` | string | no | `once` | How long the discount applies to a subscription. One of `once`, `repeating`, `forever`. |
| `duration_in_months` | integer | no | — | For `duration: repeating`, the number of months. |
